stories.Headline: California Attorney General subpoenas Nvidia over potential chip leaks and CEO misconduct
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the top executive of Nvidia last week after admitting to a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. The sixty three year old co-founded the Santa Clara company in 1993 but stepped down following the revelation of his affair. He also allegedly had a second affair with the vice president of healthcare and a third with another subordinate employee. California Attorney General Rob Bonta served the multitrillion dollar company with an investigative subpoena on Thursday, November 19, 2026. This legal action seeks to determine if the company misled the public and investors regarding the handling of this scandal.

The subpoena asks if confidential information or advanced artificial intelligence chips were sent to China, which would violate national security interests. Bonta is evaluating if Nvidia violated California law, similar to a lawsuit his office filed against OpenAI over misleading claims. The board appointed Colette Kress, the chief financial officer and executive vice president since 2013, to serve as interim CEO. On Tuesday, the company reported third quarter revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, which is an increase of 103 percent. Nvidia also stopped reporting its Singapore revenue separately just as scrutiny of the Singaporean company Megaspeed began to arise.

Attorney General Rob Bonta stated that companies cannot mislead their investors and that the conduct of Huang and Nvidia raises red flags. Nvidia launched an internal investigation and claimed there is no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised. Chairman Harvey C. Jones said the board unanimously accepted the resignation and acted in the best interest of all stakeholders. Jensen Huang posted on X that he made serious mistakes in his personal life and did not meet expected standards. He stated he would be honored to return as CEO to help the company navigate complex geopolitical and market dynamics.

Over 180,000 people signed a petition for the return of Huang, an effort supported by Elon Musk and other tech executives. President Donald Trump believes the former CEO had no idea he was targeted by a spy, though the FBI is investigating. House Democrats are investigating if Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick improperly influenced the chip business because his family has holdings in Nvidia. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the Commerce Department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed over possible violations of export rules. The shake up has rattled markets and raised questions about whether the U.S. Commerce Department was complicit or incompetent.

The Commerce Department is conducting a years long investigation into Megaspeed for allegedly skirting export rules governing the powerful AI chips. This investigation included an interview with Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed chief executive and the woman with whom Jensen Huang had an affair. U.S. intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang may be a Chinese spy, and she left her role at Megaspeed in 2025. Megaspeed is conducting its own internal investigation into the matter while the Justice Department pursues criminal conduct. The Commerce Department claims a strong track record of bringing semiconductor smugglers to justice through its own excellent work.

The board confirmed on Tuesday that Jensen Huang would not be reinstated as CEO despite calls from President Trump and his allies. Democrats in Congress will gain greater investigative and subpoena powers in January after winning control of both chambers in midterm elections. The California Department of Justice has not released further information regarding the current status of its investigation into the company. It remains open whether the Commerce Department's failure to blacklist Megaspeed was a result of incompetence or intentional influence. The articles leave unresolved whether any specific confidential data or advanced chips actually reached China through these romantic relationships.

stories.Headline: Worried About Nvidia? 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks That May Be Safer Buys Right Now
stories.Summary:
Cerebras Systems went public in May 2026, and its stock spiked 68% on the first day of trading, then slid significantly, and the stock was down to $87.17 as of 12:40 PM ET on 11/20/26. Nvidia stock was down 20% in 2026 and Broadcom had gains of just 2%, while Cerebras released third-quarter results on Nov. 12, 2026. Cerebras reported a 70% year-over-year increase in core revenue to $231 million, ahead of the $214.7 million consensus estimate, and an adjusted loss of $0.12 per share, lower than the Wall Street estimate of $0.14 per share. Harsh Chauhan wrote the article on Nov 20, 2026 at 6:45AM EST, and Dr. Robert Castellano wrote the second article, published November 20, 2026 at 6:25pm ET. Broadcom in April 2026 disclosed a long-term agreement to develop and supply future generations of Google TPUs through up to 2031, and Marvell's August 2026 Google agreement covers custom silicon programs including inference accelerators.

Cerebras designs and builds wafer-scale AI chips, dinner-plate-sized silicon wafers used as a stand-alone processor, and claimed in September last year that its CS-3 wafer-scale AI supercomputer is 21 times faster than Nvidia's DGX B200 Blackwell system. Cerebras said the CS-3 costs 33% less and has equally lower power consumption, and the company operates a cloud service powered by its own chips. Cerebras has contracts with Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon and OpenAI, added three new hyperscalers in the past six months, and signed neocloud customers for inference services. Cerebras is on track to exit 2026 with 10x the manufacturing capacity it had at the beginning of the year and will bring 700 megawatts of data center capacity online by late 2027. Cerebras expects $950 million in revenue this year and revenue to grow 3x in 2027, and it has a 12-month median price target of $207, implying a 120% jump, with 13 of 14 analysts rating it a buy.

Chauhan wrote that Nvidia may remain under pressure as investors await whether its growth can hold up in the post-Jensen Huang era, and that Cerebras' growth and outlook suggest the market is underestimating its potential. He wrote that Cerebras' slide can be attributed to its expensive valuation at IPO and concerns about the sustainability of the AI infrastructure build-out. He assumed Cerebras revenue reaches $3 billion in 2027 and it trades at 20 times sales, lower than its current price-to-sales ratio of 23, giving a $60 billion market cap, 137% higher than its current market cap. He noted the U.S. tech sector has an average sales multiple of 6.3, and that Nvidia and Broadcom are expected to deliver gains of 66% and 48% based on their 12-month median price targets. Castellano wrote that Nvidia continues to supply flexible GPUs and integrated computing platforms that dominate many large-model deployments, and that its software ecosystem and ability to support evolving models are meaningful competitive advantages.

Castellano wrote that Nvidia faces a leadership transition following Jensen Huang's November 12 departure and the appointment of Colette Kress as interim CEO, creating management uncertainty. He wrote that hyperscalers began developing proprietary processors years earlier because of the economics of computing at enormous scale, and that a hyperscaler may choose a custom ASIC for a stable, high-volume workload while continuing to use Nvidia GPUs for research and demanding inference tasks. He wrote that AMD supplies GPUs for AI acceleration and offers FPGA technology for specialized, reconfigurable inference, and that Broadcom's risks include customer concentration, expensive design programs and pricing pressure as cloud customers grow more technically sophisticated. Marvell's Google agreement contains a purchase-linked warrant arrangement with most shares vesting in tranches tied to cumulative custom-product revenue, one tranche for each $500 million. Castellano wrote that Marvell's dependence on large customers and program execution warrants particular attention, and that the relevant measures are design wins, volume ramps, margins and recurring generations of products.

Castellano wrote that training develops a model by processing large datasets and adjusting parameters, while inference uses the trained model to generate answers, analyze information or perform tasks. He wrote that training emphasizes throughput and coordination of many accelerators, while inference often emphasizes cost per token, response latency, energy consumption and serving many simultaneous users. He wrote that prefill, processing an incoming prompt, can make effective use of parallel computation, while decoding, generating an answer token by token, may be constrained by the speed at which model parameters are read from memory. He wrote that long contexts and multi-step agents increase memory and computational requirements, and that GPUs offer programmability and flexibility while custom ASICs can be tuned to particular workloads. He wrote that CPUs handle smaller models and supporting tasks, FPGAs serve specialized low-latency applications, NPUs support edge and client-device inference, and SRAM-oriented architectures provide another approach to moving data efficiently.

Castellano wrote that high-bandwidth memory consists of stacked DRAM dies providing high data-transfer rates close to the processor, and that the number of HBM stacks depends on chip design, memory capacity and bandwidth targets and memory generation. He wrote that a GPU can be used for inference and a custom ASIC for training, and that architecture should not be confused with workload. According to Table 1, The Information Network's illustrative 2025 model assigns 7.2 million merchant GPU units eight HBM stacks apiece and 1.5 million custom ASIC units three stacks apiece, producing 57.6. Chauhan wrote that now is a good time for investors to buy Cerebras following its recent slide, as its outstanding growth prospects could help it outperform Nvidia and Broadcom over the coming year. Castellano wrote that the investment question is not whether custom ASICs eliminate GPUs but how an expanding mix of processors changes the distribution of semiconductor revenue and HBM demand.

stories.Headline: The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation pledges 350 million dollars in computing spending to CoreWeave
stories.Summary:
The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation will provide 350 million dollars in computing spending to the company known as CoreWeave. This financial commitment was revealed in recent tax disclosures from the charitable organization established by the former Nvidia chief executive officer. A filing from Nvidia in June identified CoreWeave as the receiver and noted that 108.3 million dollars were already spent. The funding supports the Computing Initiative for Open Science to give researchers access to large scale GPU computing resources. This specific pledge represents the largest donation made by the Huang Foundation during the 2025 calendar year.

The foundation gave 19 million dollars to the California College of the Arts and 1.2 million dollars to the Hong Kong University. Core Scientific is building a 100 megawatt data center at Port Muskogee, Oklahoma, under a broader 500 megawatt hosting agreement. This wider arrangement with CoreWeave has a potential value of 8.7 billion dollars over twelve years with two five year extensions. The Muskogee site uses 70 megawatts for critical IT capacity and 30 megawatts for cooling and electrical systems. Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company serves as the electricity provider for this facility which began construction in early 2025.

CoreWeave stated that the charitable foundation does not directly use the computing power provided through these specific financial grants. The foundation is responsible for awarding resources to scientific research grant awardees who then utilize the large scale GPU computing. Core Scientific manages the Muskogee project with Evans General Contractors serving as the construction manager under a cost plus fee contract. The project design includes two compute data halls and one separate network data hall to accommodate high density GPU equipment. These facilities will support high performance computing workloads for CoreWeave and one end customer who remains undisclosed to the public.

Investors are scrutinizing the financial interactions between AI infrastructure firms and consumers because the sector is now heavily financially intertwined. CoreWeave investors view the foundation pledge as a sign of more demand for computing services and the necessary GPU hardware. Port Muskogee estimates the data center will generate 4 billion dollars in capital investment and 182 million dollars in benefits. Local entities including Muskogee County, the City of Muskogee, and Hilldale School District may receive 12 million dollars in tax revenue. The project is expected to support 150 jobs with average salaries that exceed 65,000 dollars for the local workforce.

The foundation assets were 12.7 billion dollars at December 31, 2025, which is an increase from the previous 9.2 billion dollars. About 90 percent of these assets consist of Nvidia shares, and the organization gave 373 million dollars in 2024. CoreWeave relies on powerful GPUs for its cloud computing company, and Nvidia is a key stakeholder in the business. This expansion is part of a wider US buildout, including Oracle's 165 billion dollar Project Jupiter planned for New Mexico. Core Scientific is converting and developing infrastructure to serve the growing demand for AI and cloud computing across the country.

The Muskogee facility was initially anticipated to reach substantial completion during the first half of the 2026 calendar year. Investors will continue to scrutinize future disclosures regarding the remaining computing obligations and the revenue contributions for the firm CoreWeave. The articles do not identify the specific end customer who will use the GPU infrastructure at the Oklahoma data center. They also leave open the specific types of AI workloads that are planned for the Muskogee high performance computing facility. No further details are provided regarding the exact timing of the remaining payments from the Huang Foundation to CoreWeave.

stories.Headline: Haigazian University panel urges keeping human dignity central to AI use and education
stories.Summary:
Haigazian University’s Department of Philosophy and Religion hosted a panel discussion titled “Human Dignity in a Time of Artificial Intelligence: Responses to the Encyclical Magnifica Humanitas” on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in Beirut, examining themes of Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical published in May 2026. The panel brought together Rev. Dr. Rouphael Zgheib, a professor at Saint Joseph University and the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, and Dr. Martin Accad, president of the Near East School of Theology. Dr. Berge Traboulsi, associate professor of history, religion and intercultural studies at Haigazian University, moderated the discussion. Rev.

Dr. Zgheib said human beings should always be regarded as ends in themselves rather than as means to an end, and that human greatness lies not in eliminating human weaknesses but in recognizing the intrinsic value of the human person. Dr. Accad cautioned against viewing artificial intelligence as a means of correcting everything imperfect in humanity, saying that weaknesses make people human and lead to compassion and generosity. He raised the question of whether humanity is prepared to place human dignity at the forefront while advancing equality and justice, particularly as technological power is increasingly concentrated in privately owned international corporations with the potential for domination and manipulation. Drawing on Paolo Benanti, an advisor to the Pope on artificial intelligence, Rev. Dr. Zgheib said technology should adapt to human beings rather than requiring humans to become more machine-like, calling for AI systems that are flexible, adaptable, transparent and intelligible.

On higher education, Dr. Accad argued that learning should place greater emphasis on understanding what it means to be human in the present age, identifying the encyclical as a valuable source for such reflection, while Rev. Dr. Zgheib called for a shift from the pursuit of knowledge toward the cultivation of wisdom developed over time through lived and embodied human experiences. Dr. Accad also underscored the importance of patience in the learning process, and both panelists agreed that education must cultivate the discernment to recognize when artificial intelligence can be a useful tool and when its use should be avoided. Asked by an audience member about using AI for personal advice and life decisions, the panelists cautioned against relying on it for matters requiring deeper human understanding, noting that AI lacks emotional intelligence and cannot fully perceive the underlying concerns or unspoken questions behind a person’s inquiries. The discussion reaffirmed the importance of safeguarding human dignity, wisdom and the distinctly human dimensions of knowledge and decision-making in the age of artificial intelligence.

stories.Headline: Trump administration approves shipment of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China
stories.Summary:
The administration of President Donald Trump approved exports of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips to Chinese companies. These sales occurred between December 2025 and May 2026, according to the House Foreign Affairs Committee. The approved chips were manufactured by Nvidia and AMD for use by various firms in China. This information was revealed by the committee on Thursday through an unusual release of licensing data. The approvals came despite previous restrictions on Chinese access to these prized artificial intelligence chips.

The Department of Commerce approved 879,000 chips, including 150,000 for Tencent, 75,000 for Alibaba, 43,000 for Baidu, and 4,000 for BYD. These four companies are on the Pentagon list of alleged Chinese military backed firms. The approved hardware included Nvidia H200 chips and the equivalent MI325X models made by AMD. Companies had actually sought permission to ship 3.4 million chips to China during this six month period. Trump gave the green light for H200 shipments in December, rolling back restrictions from the Biden era.

Committee Chair Brian Mast used the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to publicly reveal this license application information. Mast stated that this release is the most detailed public disclosure in the history of that specific legislation. Nvidia said the approvals were subject to limited volumes and strict conditions, but they stopped shipping H200s. AMD stated that it maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance with all applicable United States export control laws. Commerce official Jeffrey Kessler testified in July that shipments had begun, although he noted there were very few.

Former US official Chris McGuire said it was astonishing that over 30 percent of chips went to military companies. McGuire questioned if the Commerce Department conducted any serious national security review before it approved these specific licenses. China hawks across the US political spectrum criticized the rollback of restrictions, fearing a supercharged Chinese military. The news affected markets, as Nvidia stock fell 3.3 percent and AMD shares slumped by 7.7 percent. The broader Nasdaq and S&P 500 also dropped by 2.2 percent and 1.8 percent, respectively.

Former President Joe Biden restricted these chips to protect the US lead in AI and prevent Chinese military growth. Scrutiny increased after news emerged that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. This scandal highlighted instances where Nvidia AI chips were smuggled into China without any punishment for the actors. Meanwhile, Tencent reported third quarter revenue of 207.34 billion yuan, while its capital spending hit 81.4 billion yuan. Tencent also leased 100,000 Nvidia class chips from Oracle for roughly 7 billion dollars over five years.

The Trump administration now faces pressure to crack down on technology threats as it coordinates AI rules with Xi Jinping. It remains unclear how many of the approved licenses actually resulted in physical shipments of chips to China. Some reports suggest only about ten companies were cleared to buy the H200, with few deliveries taking place. Investors are now waiting to see if heavy AI spending by Chinese firms turns into actual cloud revenue. The articles leave open whether the US will reinstate tougher restrictions following the recent House committee revelations.

stories.Headline: Hunterbrook Capital shorts AMD over alleged ties to blacklisted Chinese firms
stories.Summary:
Short sellers targeted Advanced Micro Devices on Thursday, November 20, 2026, after claims surfaced regarding connections to blacklisted Chinese firms. This sell-off erased more than 10 per cent of the company's value in a few hours, with shares dropping over 7 per cent during regular trading and another 3.4 per cent after hours. The decline followed a report from the investment firm Hunterbrook Capital, which disclosed a short position against the chip maker. These events occurred as California authorities simultaneously targeted Nvidia in a separate probe regarding the illegal transfer of technology to China.

The situation involving Advanced Micro Devices stems from claims by Hunterbrook Media that company firmware was found in products from IEIT Systems. This server maker is part of the Inspur Group, which the US Commerce Department blacklisted in 2023, along with three other closely linked companies. Meanwhile, California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia to determine if advanced chips or confidential data reached China. This probe follows the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose shares plummeted 22 per cent after reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a suspected spy.

Attorney General Rob Bonta stated that companies are prohibited from misleading their investors under corporate securities law. He is investigating whether the actions of Nvidia or its former leader violated California law by deceiving the public. Regarding the Nvidia leadership crisis, board chair Harvey Jones confirmed the company has no intention of reinstating Jensen Huang. Huang admitted to having affairs with subordinates and left the company last week, despite public campaigns for his return by leaders like Elon Musk. Megaspeed, a customer of Nvidia, denied that its operations were used to divert chips to China.

These investigations highlight a broader tension over whether Advanced Micro Devices will become the next target after the scandal surrounding Nvidia. Members of the US Congress have urged the Department of Commerce to investigate if Megaspeed diverted hardware to Chinese entities. While Nvidia reports that its sales are soaring, the company remains in a messy transnational situation. The market now speculates if Advanced Micro Devices will face similar regulatory scrutiny as a secondary supplier for the Chinese market.

stories.Headline: Anthropic debuts on Wall Street at $1.75 trillion as safety pledges face shareholder pressure
stories.Summary:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence startup known for its Claude chatbot, made its debut on Wall Street on Thursday and ended its first day of trading with a market value of $1.75 trillion, according to TechGig. The company was founded by seven people, including CEO Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who left OpenAI to build a company focused on AI safety. Amodei described the conflict between safety and advancing AI as a central tension within the company on Thursday. The company still pledges to prioritise humanity's benefit but now faces shareholder pressure to make profits from technology its leaders have described as posing existential threats.

The listing follows a period of rapid expansion, and a report from the nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research found Anthropic is developing its systems around twice as quickly as a year ago, largely due to AI itself. An Anthropic researcher resigned in September and criticised the safety practices of both Anthropic and OpenAI, saying they were gambling with lives. Anthropic is structured as a public benefit corporation, legally obligated to balance shareholder interests with the public good, a structure the article says places it in uncharted territory because such companies rarely reach this scale in the public market. Before the IPO the Amodei siblings each had a net worth of just over $14 billion, which rose to over $22 billion by Thursday afternoon, and the co-founders have committed to pledging 80 per cent of their equity to philanthropy. Anthropic's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission last month included an unusually lengthy 93 pages on risk factors, noting that advanced AI systems could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.

Separately, the US-based nonprofit Better Data Center Project mapped 19 US sites where Anthropic has leased between 5.9 and 9.6 GW of capacity, out of approximately 15 GW it has contracted, according to Data Center Dynamics. The nonprofit claimed that approximately 2.5 GW, or 26 percent, is powered by on-site natural gas, with the remainder tied to the grid, which is itself 47 percent natural gas, so it asserted that 60 percent of the mapped sites' power demand is tied to natural gas. Earlier in November Anthropic signed a $3.4 billion deal for 1.7 GW of natural gas generators supplied by Caterpillar, in partnership with OnePWR, expected to be available within two years. Paweł Czyżak, CEO and founder of Ornaq, said the figures were estimates, that Anthropic does not disclose its sites, that at least 5 GW is not mapped and that some attributions are speculative, while noting he had expected a higher standard.

An Anthropic spokesperson told Data Center Dynamics that the company was working to add new power generation so it is not drawing on supply used by local homes and businesses, and said much of that new power is natural gas because it can be brought online quickly, ramps up and down as demand changes and is abundant in the places being considered. The spokesperson said the company is also working to broaden its energy mix with geothermal, wind, solar and emerging technologies, and is designing projects that will rely on renewable energy in regions with strong renewable resources. The company also pointed to sustainability measures including joining the carbon emission buying consortium Frontier and working with Watershed, a carbon accounting and emissions disclosure platform. The power research came as the company completed its initial public offering this week, which was expected to value it at approximately $1.5 trillion after shares were priced at $83 ahead of its Nasdaq debut.

stories.Headline: Dell and Microsoft expand private cloud partnership to run enterprise AI inference on Nvidia HGX B300 systems
stories.Summary:
Dell Technologies and Microsoft expanded their private cloud partnership to support enterprise AI workloads on Nvidia HGX B300 systems, targeting organizations that want to run inference closer to sensitive data. The integration combines Dell infrastructure, Nvidia's HGX accelerated computing platform and Microsoft's Azure Local and Foundry Local software. It gives enterprises another option for deploying AI workloads outside public cloud environments while retaining control over data processing and infrastructure. The market opportunity is hybrid infrastructure, not a retreat from cloud services. Dell announced new additions to its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, extending a portfolio it says now includes more than 420 offerings and serves more than 6,500 customers.

Microsoft announced at its Ignite conference Nov. 17 that Foundry Local is generally available on Azure Local, and confirmed expanded Azure Local hardware support for Nvidia HGX B300 systems, enabling large-scale, multi-GPU inference and agentic workloads. Microsoft identified Dell, HPE and Lenovo as hardware partners with validated systems but did not provide specific delivery dates for those configurations. In IDC's June 2026 Worldwide Digital Infrastructure Sentiment Survey, 85% of enterprises said their AI workloads require both on-premises and public cloud infrastructure, according to Dave McCarthy, group vice president for cloud and data centers at IDC. Sovereignty and latency each influenced 51% of respondents, ahead of cost at 42%, McCarthy said. In IDC's June survey, 73% of respondents said AI infrastructure complexity delays the move to production, McCarthy said.

McCarthy said enterprises are rebalancing and public cloud stays in the mix. Steven Dickens, CEO and principal analyst at HyperFrame Research, said tokenomics and sovereignty concerns are driving a hybrid AI model, and that open-weight models give enterprises more deployment choices while organizations seek greater control over data and AI costs. McCarthy said IDC expects sovereign private cloud to be among the fastest-growing private cloud segments through 2028, and identified Azure Local as a platform scaling to support GPU-based sovereign inference, with Dell among its validated hardware partners. McCarthy said the Dell-Microsoft integration simplifies some of the companies' infrastructure layers, including lifecycle management, firmware coordination and support. Holger Mueller, vice president and principal analyst at Constellation Research, said integrated platforms also reduce implementation work and eliminate integration risks that enterprises would otherwise have to manage themselves.

Mueller said that does not remove the need for IT teams to manage capacity, optimize workloads and maintain the underlying infrastructure, and that the value of an integrated platform depends on how much operational work it actually removes. McCarthy said on-premises infrastructure makes economic sense when inference workloads are large, steady and predictable, and that for large and frontier models running sustained workloads, IDC finds on-premises total cost of ownership can be significantly lower than cloud infrastructure as a service once power, cooling and facilities costs are included. Mueller said organizations that understand their capacity requirements can often run workloads cheaper on owned infrastructure, but that many enterprises are still determining which AI workloads they will run and how much computing capacity those applications will need. Mueller said there is some doubt these can be reasonably sized at the current state of AI adoption in the enterprise. Mueller also cautioned against treating data sovereignty as the primary reason to move AI workloads on premises, saying public cloud providers offer data controls and the commercial advantage of running workloads in a particular environment remains the more important consideration.

Deploying AI locally gives enterprises greater control over workload placement, but it also makes them responsible for operating the infrastructure supporting those applications, including GPU capacity, storage, networking, power and cooling, along with the software needed to manage model execution and infrastructure utilization. For regulated organizations, control over data processing and workload placement can influence infrastructure decisions, and financial services, healthcare and government organizations face requirements governing where data resides and how they process it. Azure Local provides the infrastructure platform for running workloads in customer-controlled environments, and Foundry Local enables organizations to deploy and run AI models locally, keeping inference close to enterprise data. The expanded architecture brings Nvidia HGX B300 accelerated computing into Microsoft's Azure Local environment through validated hardware partners, including Dell. The broader Dell AI Factory architecture includes modular infrastructure built around Dell PowerStore, Dell PowerEdge XE9785 systems with NVIDIA HGX B300 GPUs, and Dell-supported NVIDIA AI Enterprise software.

Dell's announcements focus on four areas: data preparation for AI, management software for AI infrastructure, partner-built validated solutions, and new storage options for large AI workloads, intended to help companies move agentic AI projects from pilot stages into production. Among the additions is Agentic Data Gateway, which Dell says gives AI agents a single governed route to enterprise data and context, and in internal testing reusing context reduced token consumption by as much as 76% and increased answer accuracy from 60% to 94%. Dell is also adding hybrid data pipeline orchestration so pipelines can run where data already sits, including on-premises private clouds, Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA environments, non-Dell systems and public clouds, intended to reduce the need to move large unstructured datasets between environments. Dell is expanding its Exascale portfolio with a liquid-cooled 2OU platform supporting up to 32 NVMe drives and a 1U platform offering 67% higher drive density per rack unit than the previous generation, and says software-defined PowerScale on Dell Exascale has achieved NVIDIA-Certified Storage validation at the Foundation level. Dell introduced Dell OpenManage Rack Scale, which it says can manage up to 100,000 devices, up from 8,000 in the previous generation, and Dell Fabric Manager, which internal lab analysis found could cut Day-2 operational effort by up to 80% while maintaining a fully accurate device inventory.

stories.Headline: Azerbaijan security official warns AI vulnerabilities expose critical infrastructure to faster automated attacks
stories.Summary:
Singapore cyber defenders faced hundreds of AI agents during a national exercise on November 19, 2026, to test their defensive capabilities. These simulated AI agents were capable of taking control of a computer network within hours to challenge the city's security teams. The Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise used AI tools to help defenders prepare for attacks on transport, water, and power essential services. A fully autonomous AI defence team was also trialled to see if machines could contain attacks without any human intervention. Noah Kong reported on these events which focused on the evolving nature of cyber threats to the nation's critical infrastructure.

The exercise in Singapore occurred while Davud Rustamov spoke in Baku, Azerbaijan, at the 2nd International Conference on Cyber Diplomacy. Rustamov noted that Azerbaijan began establishing a legislative framework for critical infrastructure in 2020, using experience from Italy and the US. Other countries that influenced this framework include Israel and Türkiye, and the legislative process for critical information infrastructure is now complete. The State Security Service of Azerbaijan is the primary authority for security and exercises state oversight over critical information infrastructure. This agency also combats global cyber threats and conducts penetration testing, security audits, and digital forensic investigations for the state.

Davud Rustamov, the Head of the Cybersecurity Operations Center of the State Security Service, spoke during a panel discussion in Baku. He stated that most AI applications contain vulnerabilities because they use a diverse range of software libraries, including some that are outdated. Rustamov explained that these vulnerabilities allow cyberattacks to leverage other AI solutions, and that state affiliated actors specifically target critical infrastructure. He mentioned that the State Security Service shares Indicators of Compromise with international partners and operators of critical infrastructure to strengthen capabilities. Rustamov emphasized that national security agencies must continuously monitor how artificial intelligence is reshaping the current global threat landscape.

Rustamov noted that AI allows existing attack tactics, such as impersonation and reconnaissance, to be executed more rapidly and on larger scales. He stated that operators of critical infrastructure, intelligence services, and national cyber centers must collaborate and exchange information on observed threats. The Azerbaijani official warned that uncensored AI models on darknet resources offer malicious actors extensive capabilities to automate complex attack scenarios. He remarked that law enforcement agencies may not always be prepared to counter these sophisticated attacks using only traditional investigation methods. These threats affect government institutions and the continuous operation of essential services that must be ensured during a cyber incident.

Azerbaijan uses a platform called MISP, where government agencies, private sector representatives, and infrastructure operators share malicious indicators of compromise daily. The country has also joined international MISP Threat Sharing platforms to exchange data on malicious software and threats with local partners. The 2nd International Conference on Cyber Diplomacy was jointly organized by the National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics. Other organizers included the State Service for Special Communications and Information Security, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the State Security Service. The Office of the President and the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport also participated in organizing the Baku event.

Future priorities for Azerbaijan include elevating international cooperation to an operational level to identify the initial signs of cyberattack campaigns early. Rustamov called for reliable, 24/7 communication channels among national incident response teams and agreements for the rapid exchange of threat intelligence. He suggested that countries should conduct joint exercises to test how coordination will be executed during actual cross border cyber incidents. A proposed unified national cybersecurity landscape would integrate data from law enforcement, intelligence services, and sector regulators onto a single platform. The articles leave open how Singapore's autonomous AI trial performed and the specific results of the Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise.

The city of Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia is currently transforming into a major hub for artificial intelligence computing. This shift is occurring as the region moves away from its traditional identity as the potato capital of China. Large areas of grazing lands and potato farms are being replaced by the construction of massive data centres. This rapid industrial boom is creating new economic opportunities for the local population in the region. The transition requires the conversion of agricultural land into high tech infrastructure to support the growing AI boom.

This massive construction effort is raising serious concerns regarding the sustainability of water resources in a drought prone area. Local observers worry that the high water demands of data centres will negatively impact the environment. There are also significant questions about how these changes will affect the long term livelihoods of local farmers. Local authorities and developers are responsible for managing this transition from farming to digital infrastructure.

They have noted that the shift provides a way to modernize the regional economy through technology. However, critics argue that the environmental costs may outweigh the economic benefits of the new computing hubs. The balance between industrial growth and ecological preservation remains a central point of contention for the community. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Economists argue AI investment outpaces GDP and may erode demand through falling wage shares
stories.Summary:
Investment in AI-related equipment has grown about 3.5 times since 2021, far faster than GDP, The Hindu reported on November 20, 2026. Indranil Chowdhury and Rohit Azad wrote the piece as the second in a two-part series. They made the global economy their canvas to avoid between-country gain and loss that AI may cause. They asked what may happen to the global pie of output and jobs. They called the piece speculative and presented two opposite cases.

Global demand consists of workers' consumption, capitalists' consumption, investment and government expenditure, because the trade component cancels out. The authors set government intervention outside the "pure" market economy and focused on consumption and investment. They defined the wage share as real wages divided by labour productivity. In their example, output of 100 is split equally, workers consume all their wages and capitalists consume half, giving consumption demand of 75. With AI, the wage share falls to 30%, workers' consumption falls to 30 and capitalists' consumption rises to 35, so demand of 10 disappears.

Rosa Luxemburg, a German Marxist, argued that machines are not an end in themselves. Mikhail Tugan-Baranovsky, a Russian economist, argued that investment can replace lost consumption demand. He went to the extreme to say machines can produce machines which can produce more machines. The authors said the AI case, imagined as machines producing more machines, comes close to what he had in mind. Luxemburg said unsold goods pile in warehouses, machines lie idle and investment contracts.

The authors listed counter-tendencies: productivity may rise in AI sectors while demand grows in low-productivity sectors, wages may rise in proportion, or investment demand may replace lost consumption demand. They said the bulk of AI investment would show up under computers and peripherals. In their index starting at 100 in 2021, nominal GDP rose 1.5 times while AI investment rose 3.5 times in less than two years. AI in the chart is expenditures on "Computers and peripheral equipment", and 2026 Q3 is BEA's advance estimate.

The authors said they had not touched the ecological crisis AI may lead to in electricity generation and water usage. They said the global North may push the crisis to the South by setting up data centres there. They said some countries may gain at the expense of others. They said the slowdown can be arrested through aggressive government expenditure, such as universal basic income or military spending, particularly in the global North. They said the whole AI phenomenon may be a stock market bubble like the dotcom or subprime bubble.

The authors said heavy investments were made expecting higher AI profits and financed in the US primarily through debt. They said debt will pile up the further off the profit-making phase is. They said if profits do not match expectations, debts will not be honoured and a domino effect may follow, much like the subprime crisis. They said rising interest rates, in an effort to target inflation induced by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, may raise debt burdens further. They cited Hyman Minsky's Ponzi finance and the collapse of Lehman Brothers, which triggered the 2008 global financial crisis.

stories.Headline: OVHcloud launches 55 AI cloud products hosted in Europe
stories.Summary:
OVHcloud said on Thursday that it had launched 55 cloud-computing and AI products running on infrastructure hosted in Europe, including access to Nvidia's latest AI chips and a workplace application that combines email, documents and videoconferencing with AI assistants. The French cloud provider said its data centres could take up to 60,000 of Nvidia's Blackwell chips, a capacity it said matched the largest global platforms. OVHcloud also announced partnerships with the cloud-computing company Shadow, with the search engine Qwant and with EUSP, a joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia that develops a European search index. Qwant and OVHcloud said that AI-generated summaries appearing in the search engine's results would be powered by OVHcloud's Olala model and hosted in European data centres. The launch brings Nvidia's Blackwell chips into data centres located in Europe, and it puts the Olala model behind the AI summaries that Qwant shows in its search results.

The workplace application bundles email, documents and videoconferencing together with AI assistants, and all of it runs on infrastructure hosted in Europe. The partnership with EUSP ties the launch to a European search index developed by the joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia. The capacity for up to 60,000 Blackwell chips is the figure OVHcloud gave for its data centres, and the company said that capacity matched the largest global platforms. OVHcloud is the French cloud provider behind the products, and it described the capacity of its data centres and the reach of its partnerships in its announcement on Thursday. Qwant and OVHcloud said together that the AI-generated summaries in the search engine's results would be powered by the Olala model and hosted in European data centres.

The article does not say what Shadow, Qwant or EUSP said about the partnerships beyond the statements attributed to Qwant and OVHcloud together. The article also does not give the terms of the partnerships or the prices of the products. The move comes as European governments and companies increasingly scrutinise where AI services are operated and how their data is handled, which the article says creates opportunities for regional providers seeking to compete with US cloud and AI firms. The article does not say what happens next beyond the launch and the partnerships it describes. It gives no timetable for further products, no customer numbers and no revenue figures for the launch.

stories.Headline: Salesforce and Microsoft launch Copilotforce to bring Salesforce sales workflows into Microsoft Copilot
stories.Summary:
Salesforce and Microsoft announced Copilotforce at Microsoft Ignite on November 17, 2026, a partnership that brings Salesforce customer context, business processes and actions into Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Fabric. The announcement was made jointly by the two companies, with Salesforce Japan publishing a translated version of the release on November 20, 2026. The partnership builds on Sales Cloud in Teams, which was announced at Dreamforce and is currently in pilot. Salesforce in Copilot is a plugin available in public preview with more than 38 prebuilt sales skills. The integrations let sales representatives use Salesforce customer context inside Copilot to analyze deals, prepare for meetings and prioritize opportunities, and to take CRM actions based on Teams conversations, Outlook emails and shared documents.

A separate two-way Zero Copy integration connects Salesforce Data 360 and Microsoft Fabric without duplicating datasets, so organizations can query Fabric data natively from Data 360 and share Data 360 intelligence securely into Fabric. Salesforce in Copilot is built on AIforce, a real-time interface layer that makes Salesforce capabilities available from external AI environments, and Copilot's Work IQ intelligence layer combines Salesforce insights with people and content from Teams meetings, Outlook emails and SharePoint or OneDrive documents. Salesforce in Teams, built on the Dreamforce 2026 pilot, brings business context and real-time insights to a platform with more than 400 million active users, with updates syncing automatically to Salesforce and the same permissions and governance applied. Miguel Milano, Salesforce President and Chief Operating Officer, said Copilotforce lets Salesforce reach the enterprise software most people use, bringing trusted context and sales workflows directly to where salespeople work, and that combining the top CRM with the top productivity platform turns AI from a standalone tool into something that drives productivity, faster decisions and customer success. Judson Althoff, Microsoft Commercial Business CEO, said AI's power depends on the data and context behind it, and that adding Microsoft Copilot's Work IQ business context to Salesforce customer data and sales skills lets shared customers draw usable insights across core business applications while preserving the governance and trust enterprises require.

Julie Sweet, Accenture Chair and CEO, said Accenture, as a global partner of the year for both companies and a major customer of each, is uniquely positioned to apply its expertise to designing and implementing Copilotforce, and that she looks forward to serving as its customer zero. Accenture is the design and implementation partner and customer zero, deploying the integrations in its own global sales organization, where it has rolled out Microsoft Copilot to more than 740,000 people and has 55,000 active Salesforce users, making it one of the world's largest Salesforce deployments. Salesforce in Microsoft Copilot operates through authenticated user access and maintains fine-grained permissions, sharing rules and audit trails set in both environments, with Salesforce controlling data access and Microsoft ensuring communications and documents follow existing compliance policies. Write-back actions to the CRM require explicit user confirmation and existing validation rules apply. Informatica expanded its work with Microsoft, offering a new Informatica Plugin for Copilot that lets business users find relevant data through natural language queries, and enhanced Foundry capabilities let developers build governed AI agents with minimal custom integration.

The agreement was announced in San Francisco and New York by Argentum AI, a premium GPU cloud provider, and Kyndryl, a provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services. Argentum is deploying NVIDIA B300 systems at the site in a fully Tier III environment to run demanding AI applications at scale. Deployment is underway at the Boulder facility, which Kyndryl operates as part of its infrastructure portfolio. The deal gives Argentum access to a facility built for the power density of current-generation GPU systems.

The 20-year, $630M agreement covers an initial 10 megawatts of capacity at Kyndryl's Boulder, Colorado, facility and powers deployment of NVIDIA GPU systems. Argentum is deploying NVIDIA B300 systems in a fully Tier III environment, creating enterprise-grade infrastructure for demanding AI applications at scale. The agreement provides Argentum access to a facility built for the power density of current-generation GPU systems and gives its customers a faster path to high-performance inference capacity. The facility welcomes Argentum as its flagship anchor tenant, and Argentum AI and Kyndryl intend to broaden their collaboration to support Argentum's growth. Argentum AI is a premium GPU cloud provider that originates, finances and operates GPU clusters, delivering dedicated bare metal GPU capacity to AI model builders, inference providers and enterprises.

Andrew Sobko, Founder and CEO of Argentum AI, said partnering with an established technology services and infrastructure provider like Kyndryl is an important milestone for the company. Sobko said the agreement reflects a shared commitment to expanding secure, high-performance compute infrastructure and supporting the growing demands of enterprises embracing AI at scale. Jamie Rutledge, President of Kyndryl U.S., said the agreement gives a unique opportunity to put Kyndryl capacity to work in an innovative way. Rutledge said Kyndryl's mission-critical capabilities and decades of operational and services experience will support Argentum as it creates capacity for its customers. Kyndryl is a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services offering advisory, implementation and managed service capabilities to thousands of customers in more than 60 countries.

The facility welcomes a fast-growing, enterprise-grade AI inference company whose technology powers some of the world's most widely used AI applications as its flagship anchor tenant. Argentum works with data center operators and builds capacity around customer demand, with a focus on speed of delivery, reliability and long-term partnerships. stories.Headline: Anthropic launches initial public offering with valuation of 1.76 trillion dollars
stories.Summary:
Anthropic launched a successful initial public offering on Thursday, November 20, 2026, after pricing shares on Wednesday. The company priced its stock at 83 dollars per share, which was above the expected range of 70 to 78 dollars. The offering was upsized to approximately 980 million shares and opened on the Nasdaq at 111.50 dollars. Shares rose to 115 dollars before closing at 97.17 dollars, creating a fully diluted value of 1.76 trillion dollars. Underwriters exercised the greenshoe on Friday, bringing the total IPO to 93.5 billion dollars.

The total value reached 119.5 billion dollars including a 26 billion dollar private placement, surpassing the June SpaceX IPO. Nvidia reported third quarter revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, with data center revenue reaching 107.6 billion dollars. Interim CEO Colette Kress guided fourth quarter revenue to 130 billion dollars and raised fiscal 2028 growth to 75 percent. TSMC approved 40.9 billion dollars in new capital and 500 million dollars each for Anthropic and OpenAI. TSMC also created a 500 million dollar investment arm for chip startups and its own suppliers.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that business is continuing as usual while the cloud backlog stands at 2.5 trillion dollars. The Nvidia board declared that they will not bring back former leader Jensen Huang to the helm. TSMC executive Kevin Zhang described the stakes in AI labs as a reinforcing loop for a larger ecosystem. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted that President Trump did not discuss Jensen Huang with President Xi in Shenzhen. The Nvidia board also formed a new export control committee to manage its complex international business.

The US Commerce Department now requires licenses for remote access in Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, and Malaysia. This move affects Chinese AI companies that used Malaysian data centers in Johor and Senawang to access compute. ByteDance reportedly accounts for nearly 70 percent of DayOne business in Malaysia, where total investment exceeds 34 billion dollars. Records link Megaspeed to nearly 12 billion dollars of chips headed to China, according to the reports. The AI sell-off spread from Asia to the US, causing Anthropic shares to give back most of their pop.

Anthropic faced a Pentagon dispute and a race with OpenAI while securing nearly 900 billion dollars in compute contracts. Nvidia previously conducted 129 venture deals this year, representing 27 percent of the global venture capital deal value. The company disclosed 530 billion dollars of gross off-balance-sheet guarantees as of its second quarter. Nvidia also provided 140 billion dollars in deals and guarantees over a two month period earlier this year. Vera Rubin shipments brought in nearly 20 billion dollars during the first quarter of those shipments.

Nvidia has stopped shipping licensed chips to China, and support for neoclouds will now be disciplined and selective. UBS estimates that a pullback in Nvidia investments could remove 50 billion dollars or more from the market. The industry is now adjusting to a world without Jensen Huang, who acted as the primary industry kingmaker. The articles leave open how the market will react to the tightening of AI credit without the Jensen put. Future developments include an expected OpenAI IPO next year and the ongoing impact of the AI sell-off.

stories.Headline: Scientists would still find meaning in discovery even if a super intelligence solves all problems
stories.Summary:
Christopher P. Kempes and David C. Krakauer wrote about the future of science on November 19, 2026, for the publication called Nautilus. They explored whether scientists still have roles if a super intelligence reaches a singularity and solves all utilitarian problems at fast rates. The authors compared this potential shift to how astrobiologists would react if an alien species arrived with all known mysteries solved. They argued that human scientists would still find meaning in the craft of discovery even if machines provide the answers. This transition would move the focus of science from producing useful economic solutions to the deeper pursuit of human understanding.

The authors mentioned that Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov in 1997, and AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol in 2016, while AlphaZero learned chess by 2017. They noted that Chess.com grew to over 150 million members and that Sebastian Sawe ran the London Marathon in 1 hour, 59 minutes, 30 seconds. Seiko released the first quartz watch in 1969, which caused a crisis for the Swiss watch industry during the 1970s, but the tourbillon was invented in 1795. Amazon Connect Talent uses a scoring formula from 1 to 5 to evaluate job competencies through structured AI interviews based on industrial-organizational psychology. These AI interviews use job requirements and occupational frameworks to create scorecards that identify specific strength and concern signals for each candidate.

The authors stated that science should focus on the challenge of tool-assisted activities rather than just optimizing tasks for society or economic gain. They suggested that humans might become like philosophers post-science, trying to make sense of other humans and the rest of life in the universe. Ted Chiang observed that we may face a world of hermeneutics where we constantly try to decipher the communications of AI. Geoffrey Hinton, who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics, argued for the regulation and slow-down of AI research to ensure safety. He believed that intelligent machines should learn from human behavior bottom-up instead of using top-down definitions and abstractions of analytical reasoning.

Other researchers assume that a super intelligence will rapidly eliminate the need for scientists by solving all the utilitarian problems of the world. The authors noted that the Swiss watch industry survived the quartz crisis by creating more complex mechanical timepieces to demonstrate the watchmaker's skill. They mentioned that physicists once told each other to shut up and calculate to avoid the strangeness of quantum mechanics in their work. Amazon Connect Talent aims to help organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people by providing candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills. This AI service affects hiring teams by separating the interview conversation from the evaluation process to limit the influence of unrelated information.

The articles explain that Frank Rosenblatt pioneered neural networks in 1958, but Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert wrote the book Perceptrons in 1969. This book described neural networks as a sterile direction for applied research, which contributed to an AI winter during the 1970s. Recent AI progress was driven by GPUs for 3D graphics and TPUs derived from Systolic Array technology to minimize memory bottlenecks in computing. These technologies were connected by linear algebra, which provided the necessary matrix multiplications for training new Deep Neural Network architectures in the field. The authors also noted that natural philosophy once separated into natural science and philosophy, similar to the breakup of the Beatles or the Bulls.

Future science may turn its attention to asking what things mean rather than just seeking the next predictive equation or molecular structure. The authors suggest that we must rethink the science of AI because the field currently faces a replication catastrophe in its research. Most current AI methods are custom one-offs applied to proprietary models, which makes many studies unconnected ephemera in a distributed landscape. The articles leave open how we will make meaning among machines and how we will decipher the language of a singularity. It remains unclear how the scientific community will adapt its understanding of how to do science in a world of super intelligence.

stories.Headline: Legora adds Teams legal intake and Microsoft 365 AI search
stories.Summary:
Legora added legal request intake in Microsoft Teams and AI search across Outlook and Calendar to its Microsoft 365 offering, and the features are now generally available, IT Brief Australia reported on 20 November 2026. Staff can submit legal requests by tagging @Legora in Teams, while lawyers can search relevant email and meeting context from Microsoft 365 as they prepare responses and next steps. Existing user permissions remain in place when lawyers use the tools. The update expands Legora's existing Microsoft integrations, which include SharePoint, OneDrive and a plug-in for Copilot for Legal. It is intended to reduce the time legal teams spend gathering background material from chats, inboxes, calendars and documents before they can begin substantive work.

Legora's Teams intake tool allows a request to begin in the collaboration platform and flow into its legal workflow, and lawyers can then use the Microsoft 365 search function within Legora to identify relevant emails and calendar information linked to the matter. Lawyers can use that context to help draft a response and prepare follow-up actions, and check source material as needed. Legora's SharePoint integration remains in beta and allows the system to use stored documents to support agreement review and save edits back to SharePoint as a new version. Its plug-in for Copilot for Legal is generally available and allows users to begin legal work from Microsoft 365 Copilot. Legora said its products are used by more than 140,000 legal professionals at more than 2,500 law firms and in-house legal teams across more than 80 markets.

Max Junestrand, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Legora, said legal work is shifting from executing tasks to directing them and standing behind the results. He said that only holds up if requests arrive with context and stay inside the controls legal teams already trust. He said that with Microsoft, Legora is making that possible, so legal professionals can spend more of their time on the judgment their stakeholders depend on them for. Tom Quoroll, Partner at Linklaters, said ensuring that its use of AI enhances the quality that Linklaters' clients expect is central to its strategy. Quoroll said Legora's integration with the wealth of Microsoft 365 context transforms its lawyers' ability to leverage that data, and that Linklaters is excited to connect two of the most powerful tools in its technology stack.

Samer Abu-Ltaif, President, Microsoft EMEA, said Legora is a great example of the bold AI innovation changing how legal work gets done, and that Microsoft is proud to help bring its solutions to lawyers around the world. He said Microsoft's customers want AI that works where they already work, and that Legora helps legal teams move from intake to finished work with relevant organizational context, ensuring enterprise security and governance. He said it is a clear example of how Microsoft's partner ecosystem turns AI into real impact. Linklaters, which uses the software, said the integration could help its lawyers make more direct use of information held within Microsoft 365. In practice, legal requests often reach in-house teams and law firms through several channels at once, including chat messages, emails and meetings, and supporting material may then sit across Outlook inboxes, calendar entries and document libraries, requiring lawyers to re-enter requests, forward files or create copies in separate systems.

Profound announced Profound for Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365, together with new integrations that connect Your AI Marketer in Profound to SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook and Microsoft Work IQ, GlobeNewswire reported from New York on 19 November 2026. By mentioning @Profound in a channel or messaging it directly, teams can ask what changed in their AI Search visibility, accuracy and citation share, why it changed, and what to do about it. From the same Teams message, they can create and run agents or start a new Profound Project, then use the Open project button to jump directly to the work, and they can also open direct-message conversations in Profound to continue working there. Your AI Marketer in Profound can find and read files in SharePoint and OneDrive, create and edit Word and Excel documents, bring selected SharePoint content into a Profound Knowledge Base and Context Manager, read email and write drafts in the connected user's Outlook mailbox, send completed reports from Outlook, and draw on a user's Microsoft 365 work context through Microsoft Work IQ. Everything Profound produces is reviewed and approved by the team before it goes live.

James Cadwallader, CEO and Co-founder of Profound, said marketing teams should not have to leave the conversation to get an answer or get work moving. He said Microsoft 365 is where much of that work already happens, so building on it was the natural choice, and that Your AI Marketer in Profound sits alongside the team, works from the content they already have and hands back results where they will be used. Sujeet Meha, VP of Teams Engineering, Microsoft, said AI is most useful when people can put it to work in the tools they already rely on. He said Profound's integration with Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 gives marketing teams a way to connect their AI marketing workflows with the conversations, documents and information they use every day, and that it is a practical example of how companies can extend Microsoft 365 to help people get more done. Profound for Microsoft Teams is available now to customers with an active Profound subscription and can be installed directly from the Microsoft Marketplace.

stories.Headline: The AI infrastructure paradox: over-ordering and under-building
stories.Summary:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India began exploring the creation of its own artificial intelligence model on November 20, 2026. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced this initiative during the CII Financing Summit to integrate the technology into the Digital Public Infrastructure of India. This move is part of a larger effort to modernize market infrastructure and improve the overall participation of investors. The regulator is currently analyzing whether such a model is feasible while considering the various opportunities it presents.

This transition requires the establishment of strict guardrails to manage the inherent risks associated with artificial intelligence technology. Beyond the AI model, the agency is simplifying the onboarding process for foreign portfolio investors and easing requirements for Non-Resident Indians. Specifically, these individuals can now use video-based verification for KYC formalities instead of traveling to India. Other changes include framing new pre-IPO regulations, improving corporate bond market liquidity, and revising listing requirements for debt markets.

Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey is responsible for these developments and stated that the agency must examine the feasibility of the AI model carefully. He noted that while the technology offers many opportunities, there are also significant risks that necessitate proper safeguards. Regarding corporate governance, Pandey explained that the integrity and competence of board members are more important than overly detailed codes. He added that the regulator is building a capacity-building network to strengthen the capabilities of company boards.

The broader context involves a series of reforms to enhance investor protection and streamline the regulatory environment in India. SEBI is currently awaiting public feedback on a consultation paper regarding Small and Medium Enterprises IPOs to decide on lot size changes. Additionally, the agency has raised concerns about Goods and Services Tax issues affecting the commodities market with the GST Secretary. Future updates will include the specific contours of a new market-making framework designed to encourage the trading of listed bonds.

stories.Headline: Wall Street turns to Black Friday as AI selloff tests US consumer resilience
stories.Summary:
Wall Street spent the week being hit by the AI trade, and neither Nvidia's solid earnings nor Anthropic's blockbuster IPO could persuade investors to put their wallets back on the table. The S&P 500 has tumbled 11.6% from its October 6 record, and the technology sector has shed nearly a quarter of its value. The benchmark has now fallen for seven consecutive sessions, its longest losing streak since the pandemic panic of February 2020. The Dow has joined the S&P in correction territory, while Anthropic's much-hyped public debut surged on Thursday before surrendering much of its opening enthusiasm, then fell another 9% on Friday. The S&P 500 has already broken below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April, leaving the index down to a year-to-date gain of roughly 1%.

Oxford Economics expects holiday retail sales to rise 4.2% across November and December, excluding autos, gasoline, bars and restaurants, but after inflation the real sales volumes grow by a more modest 2.2%. The National Retail Federation expects 182.7 million consumers to shop during the five-day Thanksgiving-to-Cyber-Monday period, down slightly from 186.9 million last year. US gasoline prices averaged $3.69 a gallon on Friday, down sharply from $4.28 a month earlier but still well above the $3.10 consumers were paying a year ago. October's retail sales data showed overall spending rising moderately and the closely watched core measure beating expectations, and Walmart and Target delivered encouraging commentary on the holiday season. The coming week brings inflation and consumer confidence releases, an updated reading on third-quarter GDP, and earnings from Dell Technologies and Analog Devices.

Stephen Innes wrote that Wall Street has spent the past four years treating artificial intelligence like the greatest invention since compound interest, throwing money at anything with a GPU, a data centre or a sufficiently convincing PowerPoint presentation about tomorrow's productivity miracle. He wrote that the market has finally begun asking who is paying for the party, and that even a blockbuster IPO and a respectable Nvidia earnings report cannot keep the champagne flowing when the financing bill starts arriving. He wrote that investors had hoped the Anthropic listing would clear the air around the AI trade, but instead it appears to have supplied another reason to check the emergency exits. He wrote that consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of the US economy, making the holiday shopping season one of the clearest opportunities to judge whether households are still willing to absorb higher prices, borrowing costs and energy bills. He wrote that the market needs a consumer with an appetite, not one surviving on discount coupons and a credit card that's already smoking.

Innes wrote that the distinction between shoppers spending more and actually buying more could become the most important number on Wall Street's Christmas shopping list. He wrote that higher energy and food costs, lingering inflation and a bruising equity correction are putting the consumer's resilience to the test, just as the market desperately searches for a growth story that doesn't come wrapped in an AI prospectus. He wrote that a bruised equity market does not necessarily mean a broken economy, but a sustained deterioration in household spending would make the earnings outlook considerably harder to defend. He wrote that the additional uncertainty surrounding recent technology outages, which have disrupted everything from banking to travel and email, is hardly helping sentiment. He wrote that investors are already struggling to separate legitimate concerns about AI financing from the increasingly disorderly liquidation of crowded positions.

Innes wrote that the Thanksgiving break traditionally brings quieter dealing rooms and thinner participation, although fewer people at their desks does not necessarily mean smaller price moves. He wrote that when positioning is stretched and liquidity is scarce, it doesn't take much selling to push prices through levels that looked perfectly respectable a few sessions earlier. He wrote that after seven consecutive losing sessions, the temptation to pick a bottom will be almost irresistible for investors who have grown accustomed to buying every dip and being rewarded for their courage. He wrote that October retail sales held up, corporate earnings outside the AI complex remain an important potential source of support, and consumers have not yet shown the sort of wholesale retreat that would automatically turn a stock-market correction into a broader economic downturn. He wrote that Black Friday is expected to attract the heaviest traffic, and the combination of online discounts, promotional campaigns and increasingly price-conscious households should provide a revealing picture of whether consumers are shopping with confidence or simply hunting harder for value.

Innes wrote that Wall Street has spent the past month discovering that AI doesn't come with a money-back guarantee, and now it's turning to Black Friday to see whether the US consumer still has enough credit, confidence and Christmas spirit to keep the broader economy moving. He wrote that after seven straight days of selling, traders aren't really looking for bargains anymore, they're looking for a reason to believe the next bounce won't be another trap. He wrote that if the holiday tills start ringing a little less enthusiastically than expected, Wall Street may discover that Black Friday has a rather different meaning this year. He wrote that the market isn't handing out medals for bravery, particularly when the sellers are still in charge of the tape. He wrote that the answer matters because Wall Street desperately needs another engine of earnings growth.

stories.Headline: Nasdaq monetizes AI agents for financial crime management as 850 customers adopt the tools
stories.Summary:
Nasdaq began charging customers for artificial intelligence agents used in financial crime management in November 2026. Chief Financial Officer Sarah Youngwood announced this monetization strategy at an RBC Capital Markets technology conference. The company is pursuing growth across its technology, data, and index businesses through these tools. Currently, 850 of the 2,800 financial crime clients use these agents to manage their tasks. Only 70 of those 850 customers are paying for the service at this time.

The agents can deliver fourfold efficiency gains and will expand to Calypso, AxiomSL, and surveillance products. Nasdaq estimates the financial crime management market at 8 billion dollars, with half among large banks. The total serviceable addressable market is 38 billion dollars, according to the figures provided by Youngwood. Verafin signed 12 enterprise customers through the third quarter, compared to nine for all of 2025. AxiomSL now covers 66 countries and 174 regulators, up from 55 countries and 110 regulators previously.

Sarah Youngwood stated that adoption and bank AI governance reviews are important steps before customers pay. She noted that the 850 users underwent a rigorous process at banks before using the agents. Youngwood attributed the momentum of Verafin to the Nasdaq brand and existing relationships with large institutions. She explained that consortium data from 2,800 banks helps the company identify activity spanning multiple institutions. The CFO also mentioned that the initial conversion to paid customers has been very encouraging.

Most of the 850 customers using AI agents are smaller banks, but Nasdaq is discussing larger institutions. RBC Capital Markets analyst Ashish Sabadra reported that RegTech delivered 15 percent annual recurring revenue growth. Capital Markets Technology saw 19 percent growth, though Youngwood noted this included pricing catch-up and extra testing. The index business grew 39 percent recently due to passive investing and demand for Nasdaq-100 products. Recent listing switches by Walmart, Hilton, and GM were also cited as part of the pipeline.

Nasdaq's AxiomSL regulatory reporting product serves all but one non-Chinese global systemically important bank in the world. The company generated 2.3 billion dollars in free cash flow over the prior 12 months of operation. It repurchased 1.2 billion dollars of shares in nine months, compared with 600 million the year before. The company is already within its target leverage range and will focus on organic growth and acquisitions. Demand for surveillance is expanding as markets move toward longer trading hours and new digital asset firms.

Nasdaq targets trading 23 hours a day, five days a week, by the date of December 6. A Nasdaq equity token developed with Kraken is expected to launch in the first half of next year. The company is launching binary options but will not participate in sports or political prediction markets. It has not entered perpetuals because it wants to understand institutional demand and see regulated frameworks. The articles leave open when the extra testing in Capital Markets Technology will fully taper off.
