stories.Headline: Clark Hill lawyers present a webinar on three emerging legal threats in healthcare AI
stories.Summary:
Clark Hill, a law firm, announced a webinar titled Healthcare AI in 2027: Three Emerging Legal Threats You Haven't Been Warned About, scheduled for December 16, 2026, from 10:00 to 11:00 AM Pacific Time and running through the corresponding hours in Mountain, Central and Eastern time. The session will be presented by Paul F. Schmeltzer and John F. Howard, according to the firm's announcement dated November 20, 2026. The webinar is aimed at the growing integration of artificial intelligence into healthcare operations and clinical decision-making, which the firm says is producing a new generation of legal, cybersecurity and patient safety risks. The firm states that the discussion will go beyond traditional AI governance and HIPAA compliance to examine three cutting-edge threats.

The first threat covered is autonomous AI agents that make or influence clinical decisions with limited human oversight. The second is AI-targeted cyberattacks, including prompt injection and data poisoning, which can manipulate AI systems, compromise clinical workflows and potentially put patients at risk. The third is AI-driven operational failures that can lead to patient misidentification, inaccurate medical records, or automated decisions that are difficult to reconstruct or explain. The presenters will examine the evolving legal and regulatory implications of these threats, including cybersecurity obligations, medical malpractice exposure and vendor liability.

The firm also plans to address the importance of continuous monitoring, meaningful human oversight and safeguards meant to prevent the uncritical acceptance of AI-generated decisions. Clark Hill lists the webinar under its healthcare industry group and its cybersecurity, privacy and technology litigation and data privacy, protection and cybersecurity practice areas. The announcement does not name any clients, patients or specific AI products affected by the threats described. It also does not state whether the webinar carries continuing legal education credit or what the registration fee is.

The page offers a registration link for the event but gives no further details on the agenda beyond the three threats and the legal topics listed. No enforcement actions, lawsuits or regulatory deadlines are mentioned in connection with the webinar. The announcement appears alongside other Clark Hill legal updates, including one on expanded Medicare revocation powers and one on a federal court ruling vacating a Department of Homeland Security rule. Nothing in the announcement indicates what, if anything, will follow the December 16 session.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prices IPO above range and lists on Nasdaq at $111.50
stories.Summary:
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, and began trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, listing at $111.50, Yahoo Finance reported on Saturday, November 21, 2026. Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, praised Anthropic's AI models ahead of the Nasdaq debut, saying he had met members of the team before SpaceX agreed to supply computing capacity. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reiterated that his company is a "big believer" in Anthropic ahead of its Nasdaq debut. Anthropic's landmark IPO put the AI company's relationships with some of the biggest technology companies in focus that week. The company's filing identifies Amazon, Google and Microsoft as companies that "develop and deploy competing AI models."

Anthropic's IPO filing says it expects to pay SpaceX about $3.1 billion a month once all the promised computing capacity is delivered. Musk said Anthropic is "extremely likely" to keep renting computing capacity from SpaceX and could seek another 10 gigawatts. Amazon is set to hold roughly 14.7% of Anthropic's capital stock after the IPO and concurrent private placement, while Alphabet's Google will own about 13.7%, according to the company's filing. Together, the two companies will hold roughly 28.4%. Anthropic has committed to spend between $47.2 billion and $49.2 billion with Microsoft, and Google agreed to purchase $10 billion in non-voting Anthropic stock through the private placement.

Musk said "Opus and Fable are great products" and that "no one I know at Anthropic set off my evil detector." He described Anthropic's executives as "principled" and "diligent," and called the potential additional 10 gigawatts a "big number." Musk cautioned that demand could decline in a "worst-case scenario" if governments impose severe restrictions on AI, and said the agreements are short-term and either side can terminate them. He added that he would end the arrangement if he believed Anthropic was doing something "really terrible for the world."

Jassy said "we're big believers in Anthropic" and has previously said customers want access to multiple leading AI models, a dynamic that benefits Amazon Web Services by allowing it to offer third-party models such as Anthropic's Claude. Beyond Musk and Jassy, the other Magnificent Seven CEOs did not make new public comments specifically addressing Anthropic or its IPO during the week, including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, Nvidia's Colette Kress, Apple CEO Tim Cook and Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock slipped to 'neutral' from 'bullish' over the past week, while chatter stayed at 'low' levels. Retail sentiment around AMZN stock stayed in 'bearish' territory over the past week, accompanied by 'low' levels of chatter. Retail sentiment around ANT stock stayed in 'extremely bullish' territory through the week, with chatter at 'extremely high' levels.

Amazon, Alphabet's Google and Nvidia are among Anthropic's investors, while Microsoft is a major financial backer and infrastructure partner. SpaceX, led by Tesla CEO Elon Musk, is also supplying computing capacity to the Claude developer. Musk said he knew several Anthropic employees from his time at OpenAI. Microsoft participated in Anthropic's private placement, adding to its financial and commercial relationship with the AI company. Anthropic's filing identifies Amazon, Google and Microsoft as companies that "develop and deploy competing AI models."

Musk said the SpaceX agreements are short-term and either side can terminate them, and that he would end the arrangement if he believed Anthropic was doing something "really terrible for the world." The article did not say when Anthropic's additional 10 gigawatts of computing capacity might be delivered. The article did not say what the other Magnificent Seven CEOs might say about Anthropic later. The article did not give further details on the terms of Google's $10 billion purchase of non-voting Anthropic stock. The article did not say how Anthropic's stock performed after its $111.50 listing on Thursday.

stories.Headline: Nvidia's 40% slide spreads AI bubble fears to stocks and Bitcoin
stories.Summary:
Nvidia shares fell roughly 40% from their October 6, 2026 all-time closing high of $243.37 to around $150 by mid-November, and the selloff spread to the S&P 500, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the crypto market. Bitcoin traded below $60,000 on November 21, 2026, with an intraday low somewhere between $55,000 and $57,000, and the asset has now fallen more than 30% since September 2026. The total crypto market contracted to approximately $2 trillion, down from a peak above $4 trillion in October 2025, while the S&P 500 entered correction territory with weekly losses exceeding 8% as of November 21, 2026. The Dow also slipped into a correction, and both benchmarks now sit more than 10% below their recent peaks, according to Crypto Briefing.

The anxiety centers on whether the trillions of dollars flowing into AI infrastructure will ever earn back what they cost, since AI infrastructure spending is projected at $7 trillion through 2030 while Gartner forecasts AI revenue over the same window at only $3.6 trillion. Nvidia sells the chips that power data centers, so if the companies buying those chips start doubting the payoff, they may slow their orders. The selling pressure on Bitcoin appears to reflect a broad, macro-driven liquidity squeeze rather than any problem specific to crypto, and no major exchange failure or protocol exploit is behind the move. Instead, Bitcoin is trading like a high-beta risk asset that moves with tech stocks, so when investors pull money out of speculative growth bets, digital assets tend to get swept up in the same tide.

The article was written by Diego Almada Lopez and edited by him, and it states that the gap between projected AI spending and forecast revenue is unlikely to close quickly, calling a $7 trillion capex bill against $3.6 trillion in expected revenue a structural mismatch rather than a quarterly blip. It says each new earnings report from chipmakers and cloud providers will be read as evidence for or against the bubble thesis. For crypto traders, the key signal may sit outside crypto entirely, because as long as Bitcoin trades in step with the Nasdaq and the S&P 500, the path of the AI trade could help set the direction for digital assets too. The article carries a disclosure that all content is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice.

stories.Headline: Higher-income parents more often encourage kids to use AI for schoolwork, RAND finds
stories.Summary:
A report from the research group RAND, published in Education Week on November 20, 2026, found a connection between how much money parents make and how often their kids use AI for schoolwork. The report was written by Arianna Prothero. RAND surveyed nationally representative groups of parents and teens in the winter and spring of 2025 and the spring of 2026. The more parents earn, the more likely they are to use AI themselves and encourage their kids to use it to complete schoolwork. Parental encouragement is positively correlated with teens’ AI use.

There was a 15-percentage-point gap in AI use among high- and low-income parents in February 2025, with the former using AI more. That gap grew to 21 percentage points in May 2026, even as AI use increased among all income groups. About two-thirds of parents who made $150,000 a year or more said in the most recent survey they had encouraged their kids to use AI for schoolwork compared with just under half of parents making less than $50,000. Nearly 1 in 5 parents in that highest-income category (17%) encourage their kids to use AI whenever possible within school rules. Four in 10 teens reported in May 2025 that they used AI to complete schoolwork, rising to nearly 5 in 10 a year later.

Heather Schwartz, the vice president and director of education, employment, and infrastructure for RAND, said the report shows parents are encouraging their children to use AI for school in greater numbers than might have been realized. She said parents therefore need messages about when AI can be helpful and when AI is harmful. Schwartz said many students are unfamiliar with their schools’ AI policies, if they even exist. She said schools should have coherent AI policies and communicate them to parents, and need buildingwide rules rather than depend on teachers to craft their own in individual classrooms. Schwartz said the all-essential ingredient is how higher-income teens are using AI, and that if teens are using AI to do the work for them, this could harm highest-income teens’ performance.

Among parents who don’t think that AI harms their kids’ critical thinking, most encouraged AI use, but even among parents who believe that AI use undermines critical thinking, more than half (53%) still encouraged their kids to use it. In a subset of survey data that matched parents with their own children, which was not a nationally representative sample, teens whose parents reported frequent AI use were more likely to use the technology themselves to help with homework than their peers whose parents didn’t use AI (63% vs. 40%). Teens from high-income families were more likely than their peers to use AI for schoolwork: 57% of teens in the highest-income families (those making more than $150,000 a year) reported using AI to do their homework in 2026 compared with 43% of teens from the lowest-income families (those making less than $50,000 a year). AI use among those wealthiest teens grew by 17 percentage points from May 2025 to May 2026. Teachers accounted for the loudest voices discouraging AI use, with 57% of teens saying teachers discouraged them from using the technology.

Among parents who nudge their kids to use AI for schoolwork, most say they counsel them to use restraint, such as using AI as a brainstorming partner rather than allowing it to do all their thinking for them. Teens are getting mixed messages on AI use from the people in their lives, whether parents, other family members, friends, teachers, or other school staff. If parents, friends, and teachers discouraged teens from using AI, they were much less likely to do so, but if at least one group was pushing for AI use, teens were significantly more likely to use it for homework. Schwartz said that if teens are using AI to supplement their thinking, such as asking a tool for feedback after writing the first draft of an essay themselves, that’s a more enriching way to use the technology that could boost learning. Schwartz said that in the real world, she thinks kids are using AI as a shortcut and, in general, they’re getting AI to do the work for them.

Whether this gap in AI use will harm or hurt wealthier students is to be seen, Schwartz said. Schwartz said schools need to give parents clear talking points about either recommended or mandated do’s and don’ts on their children’s AI use for school. The report states that families play a crucial role in teaching students healthy AI habits that won’t undermine their learning. The articles do not say what specific policies schools have adopted in response to the findings. The articles do not say whether further RAND surveys are planned.

stories.Headline: Claude AI predicts Chainlink could fall to $1.85 by January 2027 in a bearish scenario
stories.Summary:
Anthropic's Claude AI predicted that Chainlink faces a catastrophic collapse that could erase years of progress and leave the token trading at a fraction of its former relevance by the first day of 2027, according to a TradingView article published on November 21, 2026. The hypothetical landmark catalyst in the prediction is a coordinated institutional rejection of decentralized oracles, in which a consortium of major global banks, clearing houses and rating agencies announces in mid-2027 that it will migrate all critical data feeds, cross-chain messaging and compliance infrastructure to a new permissioned, bank-operated oracle network built on proprietary technology. The article says the consortium cites unresolved concerns around decentralization risks, potential single points of failure in the broader ecosystem and regulatory pressure for fully controllable systems, and that it effectively freezes new production deployments of Chainlink's CCIP and Data Streams. Existing pilots are wound down, and the narrative that Chainlink would become the standard connective tissue for tokenized finance collapses almost overnight, the article says.

In this extreme but not impossible scenario, Claude AI predicts that Chainlink could trade at $1.85 by January 1, 2027, which the article describes as a probability-weighted bearish scenario rather than a certainty. On higher-timeframe charts looking into 2027, the article says LINK has spent years forming a broad distribution pattern after its previous-cycle peak, with multi-year descending trendlines and failed attempts to sustain higher structural highs leaving the asset vulnerable to a decisive breakdown. Should the institutional narrative fracture, measured-move projections from the long-term range and Fibonacci extensions of prior major declines open the door to a deep retracement of the entire post-2020 advance, and volume profiles and long-term moving-average clusters that once acted as support would flip into heavy overhead supply. The article says macro conditions, liquidity and risk appetite will ultimately determine the path.

The article notes that recent catalysts widely viewed as bullish could kill the Claude prediction, including high-profile integrations Chainlink secured throughout late 2026, expanded CCIP volume metrics and a completed Moody's testnet pilot for multi-chain credit ratings. It also partnered with OpenZeppelin for institutional tooling, advanced work with LG CNS on Korean digital assets, and saw banks publicly discuss moving from exploration into production systems. However, the article says that if these announcements ultimately fail to convert into sticky, high-volume, fee-generating usage that meaningfully accrues value to the LINK token, they risk becoming evidence of over-promised institutional adoption. A sudden pivot by the same institutions toward closed alternatives would turn the current partnership pipeline into a liability rather than an asset, according to the article.

stories.Headline: Greg Abel oversees Berkshire’s expanded Alphabet stake as AI holdings dominate its $367 billion portfolio
stories.Summary:
Adam Spatacco wrote an article on November 17, 2026, regarding the investment holdings of Berkshire Hathaway. He analyzed how the company manages its large portfolio under the leadership of CEO Greg Abel. The report focuses on the firm's significant exposure to the artificial intelligence sector through specific stocks. It examines the current distribution of assets within a total portfolio valued at 367 billion dollars. The author evaluates which technology investments align best with the long term philosophy of Warren Buffett.

The portfolio holds 30.2 percent of its value in Apple and Alphabet, which are both artificial intelligence stocks. Apple represents 21.9 percent of the holdings, consisting of 228 million shares worth about 80.5 billion dollars. Alphabet makes up 8.3 percent of the portfolio, with a stake worth roughly 30.4 billion dollars. Berkshire bought 17.8 million Alphabet shares in the third quarter of 2025 and increased this to 106 million. A 10 billion dollar investment was made through a private placement in June to fund AI infrastructure.

Warren Buffett personally initiated the investment in Alphabet, while Greg Abel has overseen the expansion of that specific position. Spatacco stated that Apple is the more defensive long term investment because of its sticky ecosystem and brand. He noted that Apple does not need to dominate infrastructure spending to benefit from the adoption of AI technology. Alphabet provides direct exposure to AI through Gemini models, cloud infrastructure, and the development of custom semiconductor hardware. However, the author warned that Alphabet's aggressive capital expenditures introduce uncertainty regarding the company's future financial returns.

Large language models like ChatGPT present challenges to the business model of Alphabet by competing with Google Search services. Investors prioritizing business durability over speculative upside may find Apple more aligned with the preference for established, enduring franchises. Other market participants are watching Nvidia, where founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO following a probe into alleged spying. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead the fiscal 2027 third quarter earnings report after the market closes November 17. This report could affect AI power stocks like Constellation Energy, Bloom Energy, and the pipeline network Energy Transfer.

Berkshire first started building its position in Apple a decade ago, and it became the portfolio's largest holding. By mid 2023, Apple accounted for more than 50 percent of holdings, but Berkshire trimmed this stake in 2024. The company continued reducing its exposure throughout 2025, though it did not sell any Apple shares in early 2026. Nvidia reported second quarter revenue of 96.2 billion dollars, with its data center segment bringing in 89 billion dollars. Constellation Energy has power agreements with Amazon for 690 megawatts and with Alphabet for about 890 megawatts.

Nvidia has projected third quarter revenue of 108 billion dollars, which would be an 89 percent gain over last year. Investors will wait to see if demand for the next generation Vera Rubin platform is progressing as expected. The outlook for the fourth quarter will determine if AI infrastructure demand is accelerating or beginning to moderate. The articles leave open whether Alphabet can maintain its search dominance against new AI competitors and large language models. It remains unclear if Nvidia's leadership crisis will impact the broader spending trends of its global AI customers.

stories.Headline: Anthropic ports AI models to AMD chips in days without engineers
stories.Summary:
Anthropic disclosed that its Claude Mythos model can move part of its AI workloads onto non-Nvidia chips in just a few days with basically no human intervention, a job that used to take six to 12 months and dozens of engineers. The disclosures came as Anthropic prepares for its IPO, and the headline capability is software that rewrites and tunes AI models to run on different hardware largely on its own. The specific benchmark is AMD's MI355X GPUs, which Claude Mythos can port an AI model to in approximately three days compared to the old norm of 6-12 months. Nvidia's dominance has never rested on silicon alone, because its CUDA software ecosystem is the real lock-in that developers built their tools around. Anthropic's deal for AMD's Instinct GPUs is projected to reach multi-gigawatt scale, with the first phase set for the first half of 2027.

AMD reportedly offers a per-gigawatt system cost that is roughly half that of some Nvidia platforms, and Nvidia's share of contracted future AI compute capacity for frontier labs has declined to around 39% from previous highs of 80% or more. Alphabet stands to benefit because its tensor processing units, or TPUs, are custom chips built for AI workloads that gain when customers can move models onto them without a costly rewrite. TSMC may be the quietest beneficiary, since it manufactures chips for Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom and collects revenue no matter which designer wins the procurement fight. For Nvidia, the risk is less about losing sales tomorrow and more about losing pricing power over time, with the 39% capacity share figure the number to watch.

For AMD, the opportunity is direct, because its biggest obstacle was software friction rather than chip performance, and the Anthropic deal becomes a proof of concept other buyers can point to. The articles note risks to the commoditization story, since Anthropic's results cover part of its workloads rather than all of them, and porting a model is different from running it at peak efficiency across every task. Nvidia also still holds a large installed base and deep relationships with nearly every major AI buyer, while overall demand for AI chips continues to look strong as companies spread purchases across vendors. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Meta pauses business terms on web crawling after publisher backlash
stories.Summary:
Meta has paused proposed business terms that alarmed publishing groups over the possible crawling of websites tied to business accounts, the company said, after Nieman Lab reported on the backlash to the language. The company said it is now collecting feedback from stakeholders and intends to discuss revised terms with publishers and regulators in early 2027 before putting anything into effect. It said the pause followed concerns raised about its web crawlers and noted that it honors the industry-standard robots.txt protocol, which lets sites signal their crawling preferences. The retreat comes as the traffic and advertising economics that have long sustained the media business come under strain from AI-powered search and chatbots, which can answer questions directly instead of sending readers to publishers' pages.

Google said its News AI pilot now covers more than 400 publishers worldwide, including Axios, CNN and the Financial Times, with the company paying participating outlets to license material for specific Google News features such as article overviews and personalized audio briefings. Google is separately testing a broader model that compensates publishers according to how much their content contributes to AI-generated answers across Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode. Anthropic signed a licensing agreement with the Associated Press covering real-time election information inside Claude, its first publisher licensing deal. In court documents made public in unsealed filings, OpenAI's head of ChatGPT, Nick Turley, acknowledged that AI products were largely substitutive of publishers' work and represented an existential threat to their businesses, and the same filings showed that OpenAI president Greg Brockman replied with a short approving remark when an employee described a workaround for the New York Times paywall.

Publishers have watched referral traffic from search and social platforms become less dependable, and generative tools threaten to compress it further by summarizing reporting without a click, which has pushed trade groups and individual outlets to press for licensing fees, crawl controls and clearer rules on attribution. For the AI companies, licensing deals give them defensible access to fresh, authoritative material and reduce legal exposure as copyright litigation advances, but each concession raises the cost of training and serving models, and a contribution-based payment model as Google is testing could prove harder to administer at scale than flat licensing fees. The Meta episode shows how quickly proposed terms can become a public fight, and pausing the language buys the company time, but the 2027 timeline means publishers will spend another year without clarity on how their sites may be accessed. Apple, for its part, is hiring to build an agentic AI assistant capable of browsing sites autonomously, moving across apps, generating and debugging code and connecting to outside services, a reminder that the demand for machine-readable content is only going to grow.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia and dissolves the company's AI vertical stack
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia during the week ending November 20, 2026. This leadership change occurred as the Nasdaq fell about 4 percent from Friday through Thursday. Host Steve Eisman reported that the resignation dissolved a virtual holding company structure. He claims this event fractured the single AI trade into separate investments. The resignation coincided with a large Democratic sweep of both houses in the midterms.

The circular financing involved Nvidia providing loans or equity to several AI companies. OpenAI received 30 billion dollars, while Anthropic and SpaceX each received 20 billion dollars. CoreWeave received 2.5 billion dollars, and Nebius received 2 billion dollars. These companies then used the funds to buy Nvidia chips. This structure affected 65 percent of the S&P 500 including utilities and banks.

Steve Eisman is a longtime investor and the host of the Weekly Wrap. He said the Jensen unwind is just starting and will get very ugly. Eisman argued that Nvidia should have withheld guidance to avoid a stock collapse. He stated that stock picking and valuation have returned because AI is no longer one trade. He believes the reported quarter is irrelevant to the forward picture.

The tech world wants Huang back, but Treasury Secretary Bessent has appointed himself watchdog. Banks, private equity, and shareholders are now affected as they evaluate their balance sheets. Investors in the S&P 500 are impacted because info tech is about 40 percent. Tech-adjacent names like Google and Amazon bring that total to roughly 50 percent. Other affected entities include industrial suppliers like Eaton and power providers like GE Vernova.

Nvidia reported revenue of 116 billion dollars, which was an increase of 103 percent. Earnings per share were 2.68 dollars, representing a 111 percent increase year over year. Management guided next quarter revenue to 130 billion dollars, excluding compute revenue from China. The company previously operated as a virtual vertical holding company rather than a chip vendor. This system allowed Nvidia to fund the very customers who bought its products.

The market must now determine how much revenue depended on circular financing and guarantees. It remains unclear if China exclusions cover direct sales or illegal shipments via Asian intermediaries. Eisman suggests that 20 percent of revenue from dicey Asian entities could go to zero. Future growth depends on whether the midterms produce an AI moratorium or construction slowdown. The articles leave open exactly how much Nvidia revenue will fall before it grows.

stories.Headline: Meta's social media ad business generates cash that cushions its AI spending
stories.Summary:
Anthropic began trading on November 19, 2026, closing its first day at $97.17, which was 17 percent above its initial public offering price of $83. This market entry prompted analysts to compare the new company to Meta Platforms, as both entities hold a market capitalization of approximately 1.5 trillion dollars. While both firms are heavily invested in artificial intelligence, Meta possesses a massive social media advertising business that provides a financial safety net. This existing revenue stream allows Meta to remain stable even if the broader artificial intelligence investment trend fails.

The company reported that its advertising revenue grew by 26 percent in the third quarter, significantly outpacing the 12 percent growth seen at Pinterest. Meta expects fourth quarter revenue to reach between 73 billion and 76 billion dollars, representing a growth rate of 22 to 27 percent. However, capital expenditures of 34.9 billion dollars exceeded the operating cash flow of 32.8 billion dollars during the third quarter. Management has provided a guidance for 2026 capital expenditures ranging from 135 billion to 145 billion dollars. As of September 30, the company held 454.5 billion dollars in commitments that cannot be canceled.

Dan Niles, the founder of Niles Investment Management, stated that Meta has a social media business that generates a ton of cash. He argued that this diversification gives Meta a distinct advantage over Anthropic, which lacks a secondary revenue source. Mike Santoli of CNBC also noted the similar market valuations of the two companies during a November 18 broadcast. Meta management believes that upgrades to ad ranking models are driving better conversions and justifying the heavy spending on compute. These leaders suggest that the current investments in artificial intelligence are already providing tangible benefits to the advertising engine.

The current financial situation creates risks for suppliers like Arista Networks, which saw third quarter revenue jump 58.5 percent to 3.66 billion dollars. Because Microsoft and Meta accounted for 42 percent of Arista's 2025 revenue, any reduction in Meta's spending would hit the supplier first. Investors are currently paying about 19 times forward earnings for Meta, which is below its five year average of 21 times. The market will look for more clarity during the fourth quarter earnings call in late January. Analysts expect total capital expenditures for 2027 to be roughly 210 billion dollars.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia head amid infidelity and chip export restriction allegations
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the head of Nvidia after thirty three years of leadership. He admitted to infidelity with a woman running an Asian chip supply company called Megaspeed. This personal relationship coincided with accusations that Huang bypassed American export restrictions on advanced computing chips. The controversy gained credibility after a major newspaper reported the details of the situation. These events occurred around November 2026 while Nvidia employed nearly 50,000 people worldwide.

The situation involved Megaspeed purchasing at least 4.8 billion dollars of Nvidia hardware. Trump approved further chip sales to China for a reported 25 percent payment to the government. Nvidia contributed 25 million dollars to a ballroom project benefiting the president and his contractors. Trump held a personal Nvidia investment valued between 13 million and 62 million dollars. Howard Lutnick led the Commerce Department, which had the authority to blacklist the company Megaspeed.

Howard Lutnick boasted that he promised Huang easy access to the president of the United States. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Lutnick for delaying the restrictions on chip sales to China. Donald Trump stated that the country is stronger and that America plays games with China. Huang argued that selling chips to everyone, including China, would strengthen American technological leadership. Trump expressed support for Huang returning, suggesting that the executive had learned a big lesson.

Elon Musk and 180,000 other technology executives, workers, and shareholders signed a petition for Huang's reinstatement. Former NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder said blaming Lutnick spares the president and the silent principals. Many employees in Santa Clara, California, became millionaires through generous stock awards and compensation. Many other workers face displacement and uncertainty as the AI revolution concentrates wealth among infrastructure owners. The existing leadership at Nvidia remains uncertain about whether they should reinstate the former chief executive.

Nvidia began as a gaming chipmaker and reached a market capitalisation approaching 4.8 trillion dollars. Fiscal 2026 revenue reportedly reached 216 billion dollars before the resignation of the founder. Huang arrived from Taiwan at age nine and studied at Oregon State and Stanford universities. The company launched a 500 billion dollar financing platform for AI start ups and cloud providers. US intelligence agencies suspected Megaspeed was connected to the intelligence apparatus of the Beijing government.

Democrats may start congressional investigations after the new Congress takes office on January 3. A probe into illegal sales reportedly stalled after Jeff Kessler allegedly tipped off the company. The articles leave open whether Nvidia will actually reinstate Jensen Huang as its leader. It remains unclear if the AI boom is a speculative bubble that might eventually falter. The text does not say if the Justice Department will resume the stalled illegal sales case.

stories.Summary:
Aiden Blake, a Letterkenny man who serves as Anthropic's Head of Startup Sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, was a key part of the AI company's successful stock market launch, according to Donegal Daily. The company's arrival on the stock market set records, raising $81 billion and landing its stock price at $97 a share by closing on opening day. By closing on Friday the price had dipped to $85, but staff at Anthropic's Irish offices are still set for a notable financial windfall. Blake, a former long-time Google executive, has been working with the AI startup since November of 2025.

As one of the company's most senior employees in its Dublin office, Blake is likely to be one of its biggest beneficiaries from the stock market floatation. The company offered €8.4 million in share-based remuneration to its employees in 2025, though its public filings included no specifics relating to a guaranteed sale price in the event of a public offering. Blake is married to Ballybofey native Rachel Heeney, who is herself a long-time Google employee. His father is Laurence Blake, a prominent businessman from Letterkenny, while his mum Denise Blake is a well-known poet and writer.

The article names no one as responsible for the floatation beyond the company itself, and it carries no direct comment from Blake or from Anthropic on the listing or on his likely gain. The only figures it gives are the $81 billion raised, the $97 opening-day closing price, the $85 Friday close and the €8.4 million in share-based remuneration offered to employees in 2025. It states that Blake will benefit massively from the successful IPO launch and that Irish office staff are still set for a windfall despite the dip. stories.Headline: Meta has never announced or released a model named Llama 5
stories.Summary:
There is no Llama 5, and Meta has never announced or released a model by that name, according to felloai.com. Meta's last Llama release was Llama 4, on 5 April 2025. Meta's 2026 models ship under a new name, Muse, and its newest open-weight model is Muse Spark Open, released on 15 October 2026. Pages still claim Llama 5 launched in April or June, with 600 billion parameters and a multi-million-token context window. The article checks each of those claims against Meta's own pages and its Hugging Face account.

Meta's meta-llama Hugging Face account has no Llama 5, and its newest model was uploaded in April 2025. Pages claim Llama 5 shipped on 8 April, around 15 April and 17 June 2026, and one has been retracted, with none citing a Meta source. The next Meta flagship, codenamed Avocado, shipped as the closed Muse Spark on 8 April 2026. Muse Spark Open, with 816B parameters and 42B active, arrived on 15 October 2026 and runs on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios. Manifold traders give a model named Llama 5 about a 1% chance before 2027.

RAGyfied published a page on 11 April 2026 saying Llama 5 had been released three days earlier, with 600 billion parameters and a 5 million token context window. RAGyfied has since corrected it, saying the earlier version relied on an unverified secondary report and that no Meta source supports it. Tech Jacks Solutions published a brief saying Meta released Llama 5 on approximately April 15, 2026, as a 600B+ parameter open-weights model that can refine its own weights. The brief gives arXiv 2604.11002 as the technical report, but that number belongs to a physics paper on leptogenesis, and its Meta AI Blog link points to an unrelated hardware reseller's post about Claude. TokenCalculator still runs a review saying Meta released three Llama 5 models on June 17, Scout, Maverick and Behemoth, which are the Llama 4 model names.

AI Omni Feed's release watch, last updated on 7 September 2026, opens with a claim that Meta has confirmed Llama 5's training run is ahead of schedule, and it links to no Meta statement. The page also lists a 1 trillion parameter design, a 256K context window and benchmark scores, all described as internal and none published by Meta. Kol Tregaskes, who tracks AI releases on X, said in October 2025 that he did not think it was news to say Llama 5 is cancelled, that the new Meta lab were to build a new model, and that the Llama name had been stained from the Llama 4 mess. Bloomberg reported in December 2025 that Meta was shifting focus to a model codenamed Avocado, expected to launch closed so Meta could sell access directly. According to The Decoder's summary of that report, the open approach had lost support inside Meta after Llama 4's disappointing reception, and the work sat with Alexandr Wang's new Meta Superintelligence Labs.

Meta launched Muse Spark on 8 April 2026 as the first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, and The Next Web reported that it was the model known internally as Avocado. Muse Spark is closed, powers the Meta AI app and meta.ai, and Meta opened only a private API preview at launch. Meta released Muse Glimmer on 10 August 2026, a 30 billion parameter model under the Apache 2.0 license, distilled from Muse Spark and, according to Hugging Face, ideal for running locally. On the same day, CNBC reported, Mark Zuckerberg said Meta would also open the weights of Muse Spark 1.2. Meta released Muse Spark Open on 15 October 2026, three days after launching its closed flagship, Muse Wonder.

Meta's official AI account announced Muse Spark Open as the most capable US open-weight model to date, built for coding and agentic work, with 816B total and 42B active parameters, a 1M token context window, and native multimodality across text, image, video and audio. Hugging Face's launch post puts the BF16 checkpoint at about 1.5 TB, and Meta says the model was optimized for Apple's Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra chip using Apple's MLX framework. Meta's announcement says each Mac Studio lets its GPU use up to 512 GB of memory, so two machines can hold an entire model, and Engadget estimated that four Mac Studios with 256 GB each costs roughly $38,000. Mark Zuckerberg credited Apple directly on launch day, saying Muse Spark Open runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with John Ternus and Apple. Meta releases Muse Spark Open under a new Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, not under the Llama license and not under a standard open source license such as Apache 2.0, and Meta has not said which Muse Spark version the open checkpoint matches.

The table in the article shows Llama 4 Scout and Maverick released 5 April 2025 under the Llama 4 license, Llama 4 Behemoth announced but never released, Muse Spark 1.0 to 1.3 released 8 April 2026 and updated to 2 September, Muse Glimmer 30B released 10 August 2026 under Apache 2.0, Muse Wonder released 12 October 2026, and Muse Spark Open released 15 October 2026 under the Muse Model License. Meta's April 2026 launch post for Muse Spark says it reaches the same capability with over an order of magnitude less compute than the previous model, Llama 4 Maverick. The article says the cancellation claim is the only one the record supports, and even that was a reading of events rather than an announcement. The table grades the 8 April claim as retracted, the April 15 claim as false, the 17 June claim as false, the training-finish claim as unsupported, the Avocado-closed report as confirmed, and the cancellation claim as likely but never official. The article says the table shows where each Meta model family stands as of 9 November 2026.

Llama 5 has no release date, and the people betting on it expect it never to ship under that name. On Manifold, a forecasting site that trades with play money, the market "When will Meta release Llama 5?" already resolved No. The article says it also explains how the Llama line turned into Muse and how likely a model with that name is to ship at all. The article leaves open which Muse Spark version the open checkpoint matches. The article does not say what Meta plans to release next under the Muse name.

stories.Headline: Dario Amodei tells Jamie Dimon that Anthropic prioritizes company culture over technical talent in hiring
stories.Summary:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon to discuss his strict hiring philosophy. This conversation occurred a few days before the company launched its 1.4 trillion dollar initial public offering. Amodei explained how he prioritizes company culture over raw technical ability to keep the firm unified. He stated that this approach has been a non-negotiable rule since the company first began. The CEO still spends much of his own time focusing on talent and culture.

The company requires every candidate to go through a mandatory culture interview to protect how teams work. Amodei and six co-founders agreed on day one to prioritize these values after leaving their previous firm. Anthropic screens out jerks, spotlight-stealers, and people who have no indifference to public benefit. Dario Amodei is 43 and holds a PhD in biophysics and computational neuroscience from Princeton University. Daniela Amodei is 39 and graduated with an English degree from the University of California, Santa Cruz.

Dario Amodei told Dimon that turning down deeply talented people who do not fit the culture is disciplined. He said that sticking to these standards consistently creates a team where everyone is on the same side. Amodei noted that it is painful in the short run to pass up top technical talent. He explained that companies struggle when incredible teams work against each other instead of working together. The CEO believes that internal fighting wastes the energy of a highly skilled workforce.

The hiring process affects brilliant engineers who are rejected despite their skills because they are considered jerks. Amodei believes that people who try to steal the show do not work well with others. He argues that the company must avoid those who are not oriented toward the public benefit. Daniela Amodei stated that developing artificial intelligence with safety in mind was a central goal for founders. She told ABC News that AI could help in healthcare and with fighting various diseases.

Dario and Daniela Amodei founded Anthropic in 2021 with five other former colleagues from the rival OpenAI. Dario previously worked at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and at the Google Brain AI lab. He later served as VP of research at OpenAI and helped develop GPT-2 and GPT-3 models. Daniela worked at Stripe as a risk manager and served as VP of safety and policy. She also worked on the campaign for former Pennsylvania congressman Matt Cartwright and spent time on Capitol Hill.

Anthropic will begin publicly trading on Thursday in one of the biggest market debuts in history. Dario Amodei has clashed with the Trump administration over the use of the company's AI models. He has written essays arguing that people underestimate both the radical upside and the bad risks. The articles note that all seven co-founders are still at the company today. It remains open how the company will handle business or political pressure after its Wall Street debut.

stories.Headline: Researchers launch autonomous AI agent to analyze neutron scattering data at China Spallation Neutron Source
stories.Summary:
Researchers recently introduced DrSai-Rongzai, an autonomous AI agent designed to analyze neutron scattering data at the China Spallation Neutron Source. This agent utilizes a large language model to perform joint neutron powder diffraction and pair-distribution-function analysis without any human intervention. By employing a hierarchical framework of reasoning and acting, the system orchestrates established refinement software to interpret complex materials data. The tool aims to eliminate the time-consuming iterative cycles of data reduction and modeling that typically challenge both experts and novices.

The system relies on Agentic Context Operation to maintain a working memory of file paths, domain rules, and intermediate results during processing. In tests using Si, CsAgTe, and Bi2MoO6, the agent produced structural parameters that were statistically indistinguishable from those derived by human experts. An 18-run factorial ablation study on two high-entropy alloys evaluated the MemoWrite and CoreSkillWrite mechanisms under 50k-token context compression. Full implementation of these components yielded a mean composite score of 0.9316 and a repeatability stability of 0.9905, while Memo alone improved performance by 20.2 percent.

The developers integrated the agent with a permission-controlled data interface at the facility to ensure the secure analysis of proprietary user data. They stated that the agent can move beyond simple recommendations to become a reliable partner in complex structural science. This integration allows for on-demand analysis and automatic archiving of results within the secure facility environment. The researchers believe this technology could potentially accelerate the overall rate of materials discovery at pulsed neutron sources across the entire world.

stories.Headline: Medical students who use reasoning scaffolding before an AI assistant achieve higher diagnostic accuracy, trial finds
stories.Summary:
A randomised controlled trial involving 496 medical students, of whom 389 were analysed, tested whether the order in which trainees receive AI support affects their clinical reasoning, and the preprint by Yizhou Fan, Luzhen Tang, Mengyu Xia, Jiaqi Xu, Zijian Li, Naping Chen and 10 more was posted on Research Square on 21 November 2026 without peer review. The students worked through clinical reasoning tasks with virtual standardised patients and were assigned to six conditions: no intervention, an AI assistant alone, AI scaffolding alone, scaffolding followed by the assistant, the assistant followed by scaffolding, or both at once. The scaffolding prompted students to reflect on and evaluate their own reasoning without giving direct answers, while the assistant supplied requested information and answers. The study ran an AI-free baseline, two intervention phases and a final assessment after all AI support was withdrawn, and frontier large language models completed the same tasks as a benchmark. Students first performed below the language models but later exceeded them following the interventions.

Students who began with AI scaffolding reached higher diagnostic accuracy than those given the assistant from the outset, both during the later intervention phase at 75.2% versus 66.0% (OR 1.73, 95% CIs [1.12, 2.68]) and after withdrawal at 24.6% versus 14.4% (OR 2.19, 95% CIs [1.15, 4.14]). After withdrawal, the scaffold-first groups were the only ones to outperform both unsupported students, at 24.5, 24.7% versus 9.0% (ORs 3.77, 3.87, 95% CIs [1.25, 12.00]), and the language models, at 24.5, 24.7% versus 8.6% (ORs 3.48, 3.50, 95% CIs [1.22, 9.89]). Introducing the assistant after scaffolding lowered intrinsic cognitive load (t(50) = 3.25, p BH = .006, Cohen’s d z = 0.46, 95% CIs [0.17, 0.75]) and raised metacognitive evaluation (t(50) = 3.11, p BH = .019, Cohen’s d z = 0.44, 95% CIs [0.15, 0.73]). The authors state that there is no competing interest and provide supplementary information in an appendix file.

The authors conclude that their findings support a staged and human-first approach to AI use in medical training, in which reasoning-focused scaffolding comes before answer-providing assistance. They say this order strengthens diagnostic performance both while AI-supported learning is under way and after AI support is withdrawn. The abstract frames the question as whether trainees can develop the clinical reasoning needed to use generative AI effectively and independently, given that such tools could improve physicians' clinical performance. Because the paper is a preprint, it has not been peer reviewed by a journal, and the articles give no further details on publication or follow-up work.

stories.Headline: Researchers propose Onsager-based neural time-stepping framework for gradient-flow PDEs
stories.Summary:
Zhonghua Qiao, Xianmin Xu, Rukang You and Tao Zhou posted a paper to the arXiv preprint server on 21 November 2026 that proposes a unified Onsager-based neural time-stepping framework, which they call ONTS, for solving gradient-flow partial differential equations with conserved and nonconserved dynamics. Unlike conventional neural time-stepping methods that directly parameterize the evolving state, the framework uses spatial neural networks to approximate the Onsager process variables, namely the rates in nonconserved systems and the fluxes in conserved systems. Within this Eulerian framework, the authors develop three complementary schemes: an explicit least-squares scheme called E-ONTS, an implicit variational scheme called I-ONTS, and a predictor-corrector scheme called PC-ONTS that combines explicit prediction with safeguarded implicit correction. The paper is listed as arXiv identifier 2611.20563.

For conserved systems, the flux-based formulation guarantees discrete mass conservation under periodic or no-flux boundary conditions, according to the abstract. The authors also rigorously establish unconditional discrete energy stability for the implicit schemes, provided that a suitable descent criterion is satisfied, without requiring global minimization of the neural variational objective. Numerical experiments for the heat, Allen-Cahn, Cahn-Hilliard, Fokker-Planck, and coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and structure-preserving properties of the proposed framework. The abstract does not give numerical error values or timing results for those experiments.

The paper is credited to Zhonghua Qiao, Xianmin Xu, Rukang You and Tao Zhou, and the arXiv listing names Qiao and two other authors in its byline for the PDF. The abstract states that the framework is unified and that the implicit schemes carry unconditional discrete energy stability under a suitable descent criterion. It describes the three schemes as complementary and the numerical experiments as showing accuracy, robustness and structure-preserving properties. The articles do not include separate comments from the authors beyond the abstract text.

The context given in the articles is limited to the abstract and the standard arXivLabs boilerplate about openness, community, excellence and user data privacy. The articles do not say whether the paper has been peer reviewed, accepted at a conference or journal, or revised since posting. They also do not describe planned follow-up work, code release, or applications beyond the five equation families named in the abstract. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Researchers present MAGE framework for transferable multimodal graph learning without target-domain parameter updates
stories.Summary:
Haiyang Jiang, Tong Chen, Xinyi Gao, Hao Wang and Hongzhi Yin posted a paper to the arXiv preprint server on 21 November 2026 describing a framework they call MAGE, which stands for Meta-path Adaptive Graph Evidence Prompting, and which is built for transferable multimodal graph learning. Multimodal graphs combine textual and visual attributes with relational structures, giving a rich representation of complex real-world data, and the authors argue that models trained on source graphs need to generalize to unseen graph domains so that graph models can be broadly applied and reused. The authors say this is hard because cross-modal interactions among neighbors and the neighboring information needed for prediction can vary across target nodes and graph domains. They frame the problem as two key challenges, adaptive cross-modal neighborhood fusion, which captures and integrates cross-modal interactions among neighbors to accommodate variation across nodes and domains, and target-specific evidence selection, which identifies the neighboring textual and visual information each target node needs to support prediction by a large language model. MAGE represents textual and visual node views separately in a heterogeneous graph and introduces two complementary components.

Meta-path Adaptive Multimodal Propagation, or MAMP, adaptively aggregates neighborhood information along heterogeneous meta-paths and compresses it into graph-aware soft tokens. Evidence-Guided Instruction Tuning, or EGIT, selects relevant neighboring evidence for each query and incorporates its graph-aware representations into instructions for a frozen multimodal large language model. Together, the authors say, these components support transfer from multiple source graphs to unseen target graphs without any parameter updates on the target domains. The authors report experiments with three source graphs and four unseen target graphs that show strong cross-domain transfer performance on node classification and link prediction, again without requiring parameter updates on the target domains. The paper lists five authors, Haiyang Jiang, Tong Chen, Xinyi Gao, Hao Wang and Hongzhi Yin, and is identified on arXiv as 2611.20449.

The abstract presents the work as a response to the two challenges of adaptive cross-modal neighborhood fusion and target-specific evidence selection, and it describes the frozen multimodal language model as the component that receives the selected evidence through instructions. The posting page offers the paper as a PDF, as experimental HTML and as TeX source, and it also carries the standard arXivLabs notice about collaborators who develop and share features on the site. The articles do not say what happens next, beyond the posting of the preprint and the results the authors report. No venue, publication date or peer review outcome is given, and the articles do not describe any deployment or follow-up work. The only stated plan is the framework itself, which the authors present as a way to transfer from multiple source graphs to unseen target graphs without target-domain parameter updates.

Articles.Title: MAGE: Meta-path Adaptive Graph Evidence for Transferable Multimodal Graph Learning

stories.Headline: Researchers replicate and extend weight-space programming in frontier LLMs
stories.Summary:
Researchers at MIT had recently reported that GPT-6 Astra, a frontier large language model, could write the weights of small neural networks directly in a single reply and could read the raw weights of small networks to say what they were trained to do. In a three-day sprint, Roksana Goworek, Alexander Hickey, Federico Nanni and Martin O'Reilly replicated and extended those results, posting their paper on arXiv on 21 November 2026. Their first finding is that writing weights reproduces, because Astra's networks for the game Breakout scored 514, 550 and 307 against MIT's 517 and scored just as well on two modified versions of Breakout. Claude Opus 5.5 can also write working networks, but it often runs out of output tokens before finishing. The new element is translating programs into weights, since earlier models could write a good policy as code a generation before they could write network weights.

The networks the models write behave like compiled programs, and two models independently decompiled Astra's Breakout network into Python that matched its actions in all tested states. On classifying handwritten digits, Astra's networks scored 50% on average, which is below a simple classifier at 82%. Reading weights turns out to be mostly reading the input layer, because Astra and Opus 5.5 identify which game a network plays almost perfectly. On three new games the team designed and trained themselves, Astra recovered where things are on the board while mostly missing how the game works. Auditing from weights alone is possible but shallow, because without executing code Astra picked out a small language model poisoned during training in 10 of 10 runs and one poisoned by extra training afterwards in 7 of 10.

Astra also flagged a malicious adapter in 23 of 32 cases, but it never identified the trigger or the malicious behaviour. Open-weight models lag behind on these tasks. The authors conclude from this early study that LLMs can read and write small networks, but that this currently amounts to compiling hand-designed programs and reading the layout of the input layer. They describe it as a promising but early tool for interpretability.

Articles.Title: Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers

stories.Headline: Fang, Wang, Zeng and Zhou stabilize variance in Gaussian smoothing estimators for high-order derivatives
stories.Summary:
Shuixin Fang, Xuerui Wang, Hang Zeng and Tao Zhou posted a paper on arXiv on 21 November 2026 describing a variance stabilization technique for Gaussian smoothing estimators of high-order partial derivatives. The authors note that computing high-order partial derivatives in high dimensions by automatic differentiation can be costly in both computation and memory. Stein's identity offers an alternative through Gaussian smoothing, but the variance of the resulting estimators can diverge as the step size tends to zero, even with antithetic sampling. Their method extends antithetic sampling from a reflection pair to n equally spaced points on a circle in the complex plane.

Under local analyticity, the authors prove that when n is at least the derivative order, the bias is of order O of sigma to the n and the variance remains bounded as the smoothing step size sigma tends to zero. Numerical experiments support these predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the estimator in physics-informed neural networks for polyharmonic and Cahn-Hilliard equations. The technique mitigates the bias-variance trade-off in smoothing-based derivative estimation and is useful for physics-informed neural networks solving high-order partial differential equations. The paper is listed as arXiv 2611.19909.

The work is credited to the four named authors, and the abstract presents the variance stabilization claim and the bounded-variance result as their contribution. The abstract states that the bias is of order O of sigma to the n when n is at least the derivative order, and that the variance stays bounded as sigma tends to zero. The authors report that numerical experiments support these predictions and show the estimator working in physics-informed neural networks for polyharmonic and Cahn-Hilliard equations. They describe the technique as mitigating the bias-variance trade-off in smoothing-based derivative estimation.

The context given in the abstract is the high cost of computing high-order partial derivatives in high dimensions by automatic differentiation, in both computation and memory. Stein's identity is presented as an alternative through Gaussian smoothing, with the drawback that estimator variance can diverge as the step size tends to zero, even with antithetic sampling. The proposed fix moves antithetic sampling from a reflection pair to n equally spaced points on a circle in the complex plane. The abstract does not say what happens next beyond the reported experiments and the stated usefulness for physics-informed neural networks solving high-order partial differential equations.

stories.Headline: Researchers present BTG framework for multilingual translation in cross-border firms
stories.Summary:
Jinsheng Wei, Song Cheng, Bo Xiao and Ke Zeng posted a paper on arXiv on 21 November 2026 describing a data-centric framework called Bridging the Terminology Gap, or BTG, for multilingual translation in cross-border corporations. The authors say multilingual translation for cross-border enterprise collaboration is held back by insufficient domain-specific terminology, rigid terminology translation, weak instruction-following and high inference latency in long-instruction scenarios. Their framework first mines cross-lingual term alignments from domain documents and uses large language models to synthesize terminology-rich parallel corpora. A hybrid filtering strategy that combines heuristics with XCOMET scoring is then used to keep the data faithful, and a two-stage training paradigm follows. The two-stage training starts with supervised fine-tuning for targeted terminology injection and is followed by reinforcement learning to refine output preferences, which the authors say balances domain knowledge integration with model reliability.

The paper reports extensive offline evaluations using measures such as XCOMET, GEMBA and Acc@T, alongside online human assessments, and says these show significant improvements in terminology accuracy and instruction-following capabilities. The authors state that the framework is now deployed on their cross-border collaboration platform. The abstract does not give the size of the corpora, the scores achieved or the dates of the evaluations. The four authors present BTG as a response to the barriers listed in their abstract, and they describe the combination of mined alignments, synthesized corpora, hybrid filtering and two-stage training as the way their framework overcomes them. They say the offline and online results validate the effectiveness of the framework, and they point to its deployment on the cross-border collaboration platform as evidence of that validation.

The paper appears on arXiv under the identifier 2611.19858, and the listing offers a PDF, experimental HTML and TeX source. Beyond the abstract, the articles give no further statements from the authors. The context the articles provide is the growing demand for seamless cross-border enterprise collaboration as globalization accelerates, which the authors say multilingual translation has not kept up with. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the deployment already described, and they give no further plans, timelines or follow-up work. No independent evaluation or outside comment on the framework appears in the material.

Articles.Title: Bridging the Terminology Gap: A Data-Centric Alignment Framework for Multilingual Translation in Cross-Border Corporation

stories.headline_source: Bridging the Terminology Gap: A Data-Centric Alignment Framework for Multilingual Translation in Cross-Border Corporation

stories.Headline: Researchers introduce Glance-ETD framework to reduce visual tokens in multimodal large language models
stories.Summary:
Yuxuan Wang and nine other researchers introduced a new token reduction framework called Glance-ETD on November 21, 2026. This system addresses the high computational costs of the prefill stage in multimodal large language models by reducing visual tokens. The authors developed a two-stage process that uses a lightweight question-conditioned scorer to identify relevant image regions. This method prevents the loss of small but critical details that often occur during extreme token compression.

The first stage utilizes a glance encoder to view images at low resolution before re-encoding specific regions at native resolution. The second stage employs Evidence-Tempered Diversity to select final tokens by balancing scene coverage with predicted evidence. When applied to Qwen3.5-4B, the framework retains 91.6% of full-token performance while using only 5% of the original visual tokens. It outperforms the LT-OPD method by 17.3 points and improves the time to first token on 4K images by 3.1x.

The research team explained that their single-rollout self-distillation recipe allows the model to be trained efficiently with the glance encoder. They noted that the system generalizes well across three other multimodal models and performs particularly well on text-rich document benchmarks. By combining diversity with evidence-based selection, the authors claim their approach ensures that the surviving tokens retain the necessary answers. This advancement allows for extremely compressed models that do not sacrifice significant accuracy on fourteen different benchmarks.

Articles.Title: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs

stories.headline_source: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs

stories.Headline: Researchers find on-policy distillation transfers teacher backdoors to student models
stories.Summary:
Zane Fu, Yanzhao Zheng, Ziting Qin, Qianshan Wei, Yi Yu, Gongli Xi, Jihuai Zhu, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Ruohui Huang and Gang Yu posted a paper on arXiv on 21 November 2026 describing a new security risk in on-policy distillation, a method for post-training large language models in which a student model learns from supervision that a teacher model generates online. In the attack the authors describe, an attacker first implants a conditional backdoor into the teacher model through supervised fine tuning, and on-policy distillation then transfers that backdoor to the student model after only an extremely small proportion of trigger prompt exposure. The authors report that this backdoor transfer is substantially stronger under on-policy distillation than under conventional distillation methods, which suggests that on-policy distillation may provide an efficient channel for propagating backdoors across models. The paper states that whether on-policy distillation also transfers latent security risks from teacher models to student models had remained insufficiently studied before this work.

The paper's mechanistic analysis finds that the backdoor signal is primarily transmitted through anomalous differences in the conditional probabilities that the teacher model produces for triggered and clean inputs, and that this signal is gradually internalized into the internal representations of the student model during training. Building on that analysis, the authors investigate how to suppress such anomalous conditional probability signals at the source of the distillation supervision. They then propose an on-policy distillation training method tailored to this conditional backdoor propagation setting, which is intended to mitigate the risk of backdoor transfer induced by untrusted teacher supervision. The paper does not give a figure for the proportion of trigger prompt exposure beyond describing it as extremely small.

The work is attributed to the eleven named authors, whose stated finding is that on-policy distillation can carry a backdoor from a teacher model to a student model, and whose proposed mitigation targets the anomalous conditional probability signals at the source of the distillation supervision. The abstract presents on-policy distillation as an emerging and important paradigm for the post-training of large language models that improves student models by leveraging supervision generated online by teacher models. It frames the backdoor transfer as a new security risk and describes the stronger transfer under on-policy distillation than under conventional distillation as the more concerning result. The authors also describe their tailored training method as a response to the risk that untrusted teacher supervision poses in this conditional backdoor setting.

The paper appears on arXiv with a PDF, experimental HTML and TeX source, and the page also carries standard arXivLabs text about that framework for collaborators who develop and share features on the site. That text states that individuals and organizations working with arXivLabs have embraced and accepted the values of openness, community, excellence and user data privacy, and that arXiv is committed to those values and to working only with partners who adhere to them. The page also invites readers with an idea for a project that would add value for the arXiv community to learn more about arXivLabs. The articles do not say what happens next with the research beyond the paper itself.

stories.Headline: Researchers post an Omni-Workspace benchmark testing omni-modal AI assistants on 380 multimodal workspace tasks
stories.Summary:
Yuhao Wang, Yucheng Zhao, Yiran Zhong, Feida Zhu, Hongcheng Liu, Qichao Wang, Ming Ma and Yu Wang posted a paper on arXiv on 21 November 2026 titled Omni-Workspace, which benchmarks omni-modal AI assistants on multimodal workspace tasks. The authors say omni-modal agents are expected to move beyond multimodal understanding toward completing complex tasks in realistic multimodal environments, where information is spread across heterogeneous files and modalities. In such settings, cross-file and cross-modal dependencies require agents to continually coordinate perception, reasoning and tool use as newly gathered evidence informs later actions. The paper argues that existing omni-modal benchmarks mainly focus on multimodal perception and understanding, leaving complex task completion through sustained interaction with multimodal workspaces underexplored.

The benchmark, called Omni-Workspace, comprises 380 deep-research-style tasks across four multimodal workspace types and two difficulty levels. These tasks require agents to inspect and process workspace files, retrieve external information when needed, integrate evidence across files and modalities, and produce artifacts that satisfy explicit requirements. The authors evaluated 18 representative models and found limitations in long-horizon multimodal workspace execution, with the best model scoring only 65.93 on average. Further analysis identified multimodal context inflation and task-state drift as recurring challenges.

Motivated by these findings, the authors propose OmniFocus, a lightweight approach that combines multimodal working-memory management with explicit task-state tracking to improve performance and efficiency. The paper states that Omni-Workspace advances the evaluation and development of omni-modal agents toward autonomous completion of complex tasks in multimodal workspaces. The abstract does not name any institution, funder or individual responsible beyond the eight listed authors, and it gives no further statements from them. The article also does not say what happens next beyond the authors' stated aim of advancing evaluation and development in this area.

Articles.Title: Omni-Workspace: Benchmarking Omni-Modal AI Assistants on Multimodal Workspace Tasks

stories.Headline: Researchers develop TEMPI agent to improve compositional instruction triggering in streaming vision language models
stories.Summary:
Yehua Huang and ten other researchers published a study on November 21, 2026, regarding the failures of streaming vision language models. These models often struggle to execute compositional instructions because they cannot track how temporal conditions are satisfied over time. For instance, a model might recognize a boiling pot but fail to notify the user only after the stove is turned on and the kitchen is vacated. To measure this specific gap, the authors created CoTriggerBench to verify notification timing and silence using executable event plans.

The researchers developed a real-time agent called TEMPI that decomposes complex instructions into atomic event queries and temporal constraints. This system utilizes Scenario Memory to maintain task progress as evidence arrives, allowing early observations to inform decisions beyond the visual window. TEMPI achieved a 44.4 percent instruction-level success rate on CoTriggerBench, which outperformed Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash-Realtime by 15.6 percentage points and MOSS-VL-Realtime by 18.1 percentage points. To improve on-device performance, the team optimized the inference pipeline by overlapping visual encoding and prefix prefill with frame arrival.

The authors explained that recognizing individual events is not enough to guarantee the correct execution of complex, time-based requests. They noted that their optimized detector implementation achieved a 4.90 times speedup when running on an 8 GB RTX 5060. By continuously updating the scenario state even when no notification is required, the agent ensures that relevant events are tracked. This approach allows the model to handle streaming video more effectively than previous closed-source or fine-tuned open-source baselines.

stories.Headline: Civil aviation minister Rammohan Naidu urges parents and educators to revive children's reading habits
stories.Summary:
Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu on Saturday called for a renewed reading movement among children, saying books were more important than ever when technology and artificial intelligence were increasingly shaping young minds. He spoke while inaugurating the two-day Vizag Junior Literary Fest at Hawa Mahal on Beach Road in Visakhapatnam, an event The Hindu reported on November 21, 2026. He said that while technology made information readily accessible, books helped children develop creativity, curiosity and the ability to ask meaningful questions. He told the gathering that technology is answering questions, but books will help children write the right questions, and he pointed to the growing challenge of keeping children interested in reading.

He also cautioned against declining attention spans and urged parents and educators to cultivate reading habits from an early age. Mr. Naidu said children should understand the value of both books and technology, and recalling his childhood he said his home had a room full of books that was called a library, stressing the need to revive the culture of reading. Referring to the festival's theme of collaboration, he said reading exposed children to different perspectives and encouraged them to engage with ideas beyond their own, and that unlike a conversation with someone across the table, reading enabled a silent debate within one's mind. Describing the festival as an investment in the minds of the next generation, he compared it with the investment announcements made at the CII Partnership Summit in Andhra Pradesh the previous week, saying lakhs of crores of rupees in investments had been announced for Andhra Pradesh and North Andhra but the festival was much more powerful because it invested in the minds of the future.

He described the Vizag Junior Literary Fest as an important event on the national literary festival calendar and one of the major children's literary festivals in South India, and urged the young audience to return for the next edition after reading more books, telling them the festival was theirs. Visakhapatnam MP M. Sribharat also spoke about the impact of AI on reading habits and said literary festivals had become even more relevant in the present context. Earlier, Sonal Sarda, one of the festival's directors, urged children to ask questions and interact with authors and storytellers, while fellow directors Priya Uppalapati and Sandhya Venugopal Godey said the festival had brought together some of the finest authors and storytellers. They also highlighted sessions planned for parents, particularly those focusing on storytelling, and emphasised that a child's introduction to stories began at home.

Mime artiste Kunal Motling entertained the audience with an interactive performance at the inaugural programme, and the day's sessions concluded with a theatrical performance by Chennai-based theatre group Crea Shakthi. The concluding day's sessions will run from 10.30 a.m. till 7 p.m. on Sunday.
