stories.Headline: Northland upgrades Camtek to Outperform on AI packaging demand
stories.Summary:
Northland upgraded Camtek to Outperform on Saturday, November 21, 2026, and the upgrade rests heavily on what a major AI chip customer said on its earnings call. Camtek had recently reported Q3 2026 revenue that was 28% higher than a year earlier. Management guidance points to about US$180 million in Q4 sales and a 2027 revenue outlook above US$800 million. The upgrade ties Camtek's tools directly to capacity plans in AI focused advanced packaging rather than to broad semiconductor spending.

The 2027 outlook above US$800 million sits on top of more than US$600 million of 2026 year to date orders, roughly 80% tied to AI and HBM. Those orders are scheduled into 2026 and 2027, and capacity is rising toward well over US$700 million of annual revenue. Camtek is scaling new German manufacturing capacity while lifting gross margin toward the 52.5% to 53% range and operating margin toward 30% to 32% by late 2026. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St holds that Camtek's Hawk and Eagle G5 tools are already central to customer roadmaps.

The upgrade from Northland to Outperform is based heavily on what a major AI chip customer shared on its earnings call. The article says the customer highlighted how Camtek's tools are tied directly to capacity plans in AI focused advanced packaging. The article frames the shared operational question as whether Camtek can execute on that order book while scaling its new German manufacturing capacity. It adds that any slip in pricing, costs or AI related tool intensity would directly affect that path.

One alternate view leans heavily on valuation risk, seen in the lowest analysts' case, which still assumes revenue of about US$1.0b and earnings near US$511.6 million by 2029. That case only supports a US$120 price target, and those forecasts were set before this upgrade and Q3 news. The biggest operational risk is concentration, since a pause or change in spending plans from AI and HBM customers could quickly pressure backlog conversion, margins and the 2027 revenue ambition. The article says the story could shift meaningfully from here.

Camtek's narrative points to revenues of US$1.1b and earnings of US$512.6 million by 2029, based on analyst assumptions of 26.2% yearly revenue growth. The narrative assumes an earnings increase of about 3.8 times from current earnings of US$133.7 million. The article says Camtek's fair value indicates a 71% potential upside to its current price, which could narrow faster than many investors expect. It also points to 4 other Camtek fair value estimates, including one that suggests as much as 23% downside from the current price.

The key near term catalyst is whether the advanced packaging order book converts into shipments on the timing management has laid out. The article says the report includes a comprehensive fundamental analysis summarized in a single visual, the Snowflake. It offers a hand picked list of 53 AI infrastructure stocks for potential parallel or contrasting setups. stories.Headline: Deloitte and Workday host a Central Europe webinar on people and AI as a competitive advantage
stories.Summary:
Deloitte and Workday are holding a webinar for Central Europe on the theme of people and AI as a competitive advantage, exploring the findings of Deloitte’s 2026 Global Human Capital Trends report and what those findings mean for enterprise transformation. The session is aimed at CHROs and HR leaders across Central Europe and is designed to connect human capital trends with the decisions shaping AI-enabled organisations. According to the announcement, 70% of business leaders identify being “fast and nimble” as their primary competitive strategy for the next three years, and the session will examine how organisations can rethink work to keep pace with AI. Leaders and experts from Workday and Deloitte will explore the shift from “Humans + Machines” to “Humans x Machines,” combining human judgement with machine speed to create greater value. The announcement says the session will also examine what this “Human Advantage” means for HR and how it can inform the way organisations approach AI-enabled transformation.

The webinar focuses on three priorities for HR leaders trying to bridge the gap between understanding these trends and putting them into practice. The first is creating value through people and AI, moving beyond cost efficiency to explore how people and AI can work together to deliver greater business value. The second is adapting workforce planning, including understanding the “Orchestration Advantage” and the shift from static plans to dynamically aligning capabilities and capacity with business needs. The third is navigating cultural change, exploring how AI is reshaping organisational culture, what “Cultural Debt” means and how to manage its ripple effects. The announcement invites people to register to explore how to move beyond experimentation and take a more strategic approach to people, work and AI.

The articles do not name the individual leaders and experts from Workday and Deloitte who will take part, and they give no date or time for the session beyond the publication date of the announcement, 19 November 2026. No specific statements from named people are included, so responsibility for the views rests with the two firms as organisers rather than with any quoted individual. The context given is Deloitte’s 2026 Global Human Capital Trends report and the finding that 70% of business leaders see being “fast and nimble” as their primary competitive strategy for the next three years. What happens next, according to the articles, is that interested CHROs and HR leaders across Central Europe can register for the webinar.

stories.Headline: Salesforce begins new layoffs while setting AI spending budgets for staff
stories.Summary:
Salesforce has begun another round of job cuts, according to internal messages reviewed by Business Insider, and the scale of the current reductions is not yet known. Business Insider reported the new cuts by citing messages shared on an internal Slack channel, where staff discussed layoffs taking place this week and some employees noted recent reductions. One employee also reported that their manager had been let go, and a senior manager in IT compliance and content strategy confirmed their own reduction in force on LinkedIn. That manager also stated that other team members were impacted on Monday morning, while the company has not disclosed the total number of roles affected in this latest round.

The new cuts follow earlier workforce reductions at Salesforce this year, including a regulatory filing that showed the company cut 86 jobs in California on August 7. Those affected roles were in sales, general administration, technology, and product teams, and Salesforce also reduced headcount in Washington state and in markets outside the United States. Internal documents reviewed by Business Insider detail the standard severance package for US employees, under which eligible staff can receive up to 30 weeks of base pay depending on their level, tenure, and age. The company also set AI budgets for employees this week, after an internal memo indicated that some staff had spent thousands of dollars monthly on AI tokens last quarter.

CEO Marc Benioff is responsible for the company and has rejected investor concerns about AI's impact on traditional software business models. He stated at the company's most recent earnings report that the software-as-a-service industry is not facing a collapse. The job cuts occur in a year marked by investor concern over AI's impact on traditional software business models, and Salesforce shares fell 9 per cent on Tuesday. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the reported cuts and the new AI budgets.

stories.Headline: EY, Microsoft launch agentic cyber defence centre for AI security
stories.Summary:
EY and Microsoft jointly launched an Agentic Cyber Defence Centre, according to a TechGig report published on November 20, 2026. The centre integrates Microsoft technologies with policy controls and tamper-evident records for the actions taken by AI agents. It extends the existing alliance between the two companies into agent-led security operations, with the stated aim of connecting fragmented cyber defences. EY says the platform helps organisations retain human responsibility for automated decisions while agents take on more security work.

The platform applies policy-based controls to agent actions and keeps tamper-evident records that let organisations track changes and coordinate responses. The announcement describes an integrated transformation and operations model that spans identity, data, applications, cloud and operational technology. EY plans to apply agentic blueprints across these domains, using reusable patterns to connect security capabilities rather than relying on separate deployments. The stated aim is sustained and repeatable improvement in cyber defence.

EY is implementing Microsoft security for agentic cyber defence across its global organisation as what it calls Client Zero. This internal deployment is meant to validate operating models, codify controls and develop reusable patterns, with the aim of reducing implementation risk for clients. Richard Watson, EY Global Consulting Cybersecurity Leader, said the future of cybersecurity requires an entirely new operating model. Naseem Tuffaha, Corporate Vice President, Security at Microsoft, said securing the AI-powered enterprise requires a new model for cyber defence that keeps pace as AI changes how organisations operate and are attacked.

stories.Headline: Cognizant opens first phase of 165,000 sq ft AI learning centre in Chennai

Cognizant inaugurated Phase-1 of its Immersive Learning Center at its Siruseri campus in Chennai on Thursday, according to a company release reported by TechGig on November 20, 2026. The Nasdaq-listed technology company said the facility is meant to develop AI skills at scale and to support its commitment to an AI-ready global workforce. Cognizant stated that the centre will undergo further expansion in subsequent phases beyond this first one. The company described the centre as integrating modern workplace design with digital learning infrastructure and flexible environments for instructor-led learning, collaboration and ideation.

The facility spans 165,000 square feet and features 58 classrooms equipped with 1,822 learning seats, along with 208 multipurpose seats, collaborative spaces and meeting rooms. Rajesh Varrier, President of Global Operations and Chairman and Managing Director of Cognizant India, commented on the investment in the release. Varrier added that the facility reflects continued investment in creating spaces for learning and collaboration. He said associates will build innovative, AI-enabled solutions for clients within these spaces.

Cognizant maintains an operational presence across India, with locations including Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Coimbatore, Delhi-NCR, GIFT City, Hyderabad, Indore, Kochi, Kolkata, Mangaluru, Mumbai, Pune and Visakhapatnam. stories.Headline: Siemens launches Eigen Engineering Agent in India

Siemens launched its Eigen Engineering Agent in India on November 20, 2026, at the Transform - Siemens India Innovation Day in New Delhi, according to TechGig. Siemens AG CTO Dr Dirk Didascalou said Eigen can help accelerate growth in India by giving engineers more time for innovation, and he added that bringing AI into the engineering workflow helps manage complexity and strengthens India's industrial transformation. Siemens India CEO Sunil Mathur highlighted Eigen's potential to drive India's manufacturing leap, especially for small and medium enterprises. The company states that automating repetitive work frees engineers for more complex work and accelerates development. Humans remain responsible for the final deployment of tasks, according to the article.

The launch was held during Transform - Siemens India Innovation Day in New Delhi, and the pilot involved 16 Siemens clients in the country before the India release. The article reports the productivity gains of 20 to 30 per cent in specific cases and the reduction of over 50 per cent in repetitive engineering work as pilot results rather than guaranteed outcomes. stories.Headline: Hebbia's tests show GPT-6 Astra leads on source citation and presentation quality for financial research
stories.Summary:
Hebbia tested a prerelease build of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra in August and September 2026, using the same financial research cases and grading criteria for each model, with domain experts writing or auditing the criteria against source documents. The tests covered two parts of a banker’s work: finding the sources a question requires and building a presentation that follows the banker’s brief. In the tests, GPT-6 Astra scored 13.6 percentage points above the best alternative tested on citing the required types of sources, and 99.5% of the excerpts it cited were relevant to the question. It also met 97.9% of the applicable presentation requirements, putting it 14.4 percentage points ahead of the best alternative tested on that measure, and it ranked first on both following the brief and presentation quality. Hebbia’s Matrix tool links answers to the documents behind them, and users can open a citation to see the underlying document and highlighted passage, while slide footnotes lead back to the source material.

In a hypothetical example described in the article, a banker helping a client assess a strategic acquisition of an industrial-software company with roughly 2,000 files to review could load the data room into Matrix and examine customer concentration, contract terms and churn in cited cells. Matrix could then bring in peer filings and industry news to help develop the deal thesis and turn that research into a diligence summary and valuation deck in the firm’s template. In that workflow, GPT-6 Astra selects documents or Matrix cells to support an answer and then turns the analysis into native PowerPoint slides that follow the user’s structure and guidelines. Kavita Anand, a member of technical staff for product at Hebbia, said the company had been strong partners with OpenAI over Hebbia’s lifetime and that the leaps GPT-6 Astra has made in quality outputs and accuracy have been truly surprising. She said traceability is really important to users because they base millions of dollars of decisions on what the AI comes back with, and citations help with traceability as well as giving users confidence that the AI found the right answer.

She said that when looking at a data room with thousands of documents even a single percentage-point gain can yield a lot of marginal benefit, and that she wants a deck made in her firm’s branding that looks like a human-made slide. She said past models shone on one dimension or the other, while GPT-6 Astra is the first model Hebbia has seen that is number one on both craft and instruction following. Anand described what a better first draft could make possible, saying GPT-6 Astra can create precise outputs and artifacts that adhere to user guidelines and that the overnighters professionals have to pull get reduced to a few minutes of reviewing its output. She also sees a future role for agents that monitor information in the background and surface signals for finance professionals to assess, and she said getting an important signal a few hours before competitors could let users start thinking about it and process more opportunities a human is not manually hunting. Hebbia wants to build on these results to help finance professionals assess deals with research they can trace back to its sources, and it wants bankers to spend less time reformatting decks and checking sources and more time assessing a deal.

stories.Headline: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Mini multimodal model for local AI setups
stories.Summary:
Thinking Machines Lab released the Inkling 2 Mini model on November 20, 2026, to provide cutting-edge performance for local AI setups. This new multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model uses a looped transformer architecture to increase its capacity without adding more physical parameters. It features approximately 26 billion physical total parameters and 3 billion active parameters per token for its processing tasks. The model accepts both text and image inputs and supports a context size of one million tokens for users. A DSpark drafter is included with the release to provide additional speed-up at a small cost to memory.

The model has 24 decoder layers, but the 12 middle layers run three times in a loop for 48 logical layers. It uses a hidden size of 2,304 and selects eight experts from 128 per layer, unlike the 384 in Small. Weights are shipped in mixed-precision format using NVFP4 and MXFP8, with support for transformers, MLX, Llama App, and SGLang production deployments. The decoder runs layers 0 to 5 once, layers 6 to 17 three times, and layers 18 to 23 once. Each six-layer block contains five sliding-window layers with 1,024 tokens and one full-attention layer using dynamic key and value convolutions.

Thinking Machines Lab stated that this model is a refreshingly new great local model designed specifically for smaller AI setups. They noted that in their vibe tests, the performance is at least comparable with the Qwen 3.8 27B model. The developers mentioned that more validation is needed, but they are super excited about the release of this specific model. They provided a research artifact called TML-d24-varloop-research that allows users to set a variable number of loop passes. They explained that setting one or two passes instead of three makes inference faster, though generation quality may drop.

The model leads in 32 out of 48 benchmarks in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, including coding and reasoning. It outperforms Gemma 4 31B, Muse Glimmer, Qwen 3.8 27B, and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL across various knowledge and safety categories. In coding, it leads in FrontierCode v2.0 and ties with Qwen 3.8 27B on Terminal-Bench 4.0, but trails on AutomationBench-AA. Users can adjust reasoning effort from none at 0.0 to max at 0.99, with a default high setting of 0.9. The model can also perform tool calling, such as getting the current temperature for a specific city and country.

The developers based this approach on architectures like Nanbeige, which previously explored the concept of looping within a transformer model. Information moves between passes through cross-pass messages, and a gating controller decides how much input to forget or add. The router uses SwiGLU experts, and the text decoder width is 2,304 while the intermediate width of each expert is 1,152. Attention uses 24 query heads and eight KV heads, along with learned relative position logits and a learned sink. Reusing core weights reduces the number of distinct layers stored in the checkpoint while maintaining 48 total layer visits.

Next, users can run the model on macOS or Windows via Llama App using GGUF 4-bit or 8-bit quants. Linux users can serve the model from the CLI or use SGLang on SM103 hardware for production datacenter deployments. The research variant allows for further testing of variable loop passes to balance inference speed against the quality of generations. The articles leave open the final results of the deeper evaluation for the variable loop research artifact and further validation. They also leave the full list of benchmark scores to be viewed on the official Inkling 2 Mini model card.

stories.Headline: Hugging Face researchers create harness adapters to boost AI model performance and efficiency
stories.Summary:
Hugging Face researchers created harness adapters to boost AI model performance and efficiency. These researchers released their findings and a reusable recipe on November 20, 2026. They used reinforcement learning to adapt models to specific agent harnesses and task distributions. This process allows a model to be more accurate for a target harness. The team focused on real world software engineering tasks for this specific project.

The team used Qwen3.8-27B and trained LoRA adapters for Pi 1.5.2, OpenCode 2.2.7, and Hermes Agent v0.22.6. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 with the pi harness, the base model scored 39 percent using 2.9K tokens. The adapter increased this to 55 percent pass@1 while reducing average token usage to 1.5K. They merged these three LoRAs into one super adapter for use across all three harnesses. Training occurred on the Hub in Jobs using TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer, OpenEnv, and harbor.

The researchers stated that models usually target general performance rather than specific harnesses. They explained that combining a model and harness often leaves performance and efficiency on the table. By using reinforcement learning, they could squeeze more out of the model for specific combinations. They noted that the model improved by reasoning less and calling fewer tools. The team provided a reusable recipe so others can reproduce these results on their own.

The researchers noted that a verifier accepting wrong answers teaches the wrong behavior to the model. They found that tasks already feasible for the model do not teach it anything new. The process affected the Qwen3.8-27B model by making it more efficient on agentic coding. They used a custom dataset for agentic coding built with the Hub, OpenEnv, and Repo2RLEnv. This pipeline ensured the highest quality set of validated and relevant tasks for the model.

The team used three sources for tasks, including two from the Hugging Face Hub. SWE-smith injected bugs into real Python and Go repositories to add volume to the set. SWE-Gym turned real GitHub issues and merged fixes into tasks to add real world bugs. Tasksmith generated tasks from 30 merged pull requests to target specific skill gaps in the model. They filtered 1,127 candidates down to 278 tasks that passed semantic and difficulty checks.

The researchers will provide all artifacts, including adapters, GGUFs, RL tasks, and a safeagents plugin. These materials are available for browsing through a specific Hugging Face collection. The team used docker images with target harnesses pre-installed for their reinforcement learning tasks. They used a proxy between the harness and vLLM to record exact tokens produced. The authors leave open the question of what the model really learned to do.

stories.Headline: Bewakoof cofounder Prabhkiran Singh launches AI shopping assistant Save8
stories.Summary:
Prabhkiran Singh, cofounder and former CEO of the D2C fashion brand Bewakoof, has launched Save8, an AI-powered shopping assistant that helps consumers compare prices and offers across ecommerce and quick commerce platforms, according to Inc42. The venture comes months after Singh stepped down from Bewakoof, which he led for nearly 14 years, and it marks his return to entrepreneurship with a shift from building a fashion brand to AI-led shopping assistance. Singh cofounded Bewakoof in 2012, and in February this year he announced plans to step down as CEO at the end of March, citing personal priorities including health and family. His departure ended a nearly 14-year stint at the company, which had earlier drawn a ₹200 Cr investment from Aditya Birla Group’s digital-first venture TMRW to acquire a majority stake, with that transaction completed in February 2023.

According to its website, Save8 aggregates prices and offers across more than 1,000 online stores, comparing product prices alongside coupons, cashback, discounted gift cards and bank offers to help shoppers identify potential savings. Users can compare offers by pasting a product link into Save8’s website, by adding “save8.ai/” before the product URL in their browser’s address bar, or by sending the link to the Save8 app through a shopping app’s share menu. The platform lists Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Zepto, Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart among the services it covers, and its comparison tools aim to help users assess purchase costs after accounting for available discounts and payment offers. Save8 is available through its website and mobile applications, and its Google Play listing says it displays available bank and payment offers but does not automatically apply them. Save8 operates under ThousandX Ventures LLP, according to its terms of service, and besides its deal-finding tools it facilitates the purchase of digital gift cards issued by brands or their authorised partners.

Singh is also looking to raise external capital for Save8 and has held talks with investors, including All In Capital, sources told Inc42, although the proposed funding amount and the final investor lineup could not be ascertained. Questions sent to Singh about Save8’s launch, business model and fundraising plans remained unanswered till the time of publication. During Singh’s tenure, Bewakoof built a youth-focused fashion business catering to millennials and Gen Z shoppers, expanding beyond its own D2C platform into online marketplaces and offline retail. With Save8, Singh is moving from selling consumer products to helping shoppers compare where and how to buy them.

stories.Headline: AI training platforms pay $7 to $150 an hour but gate most work behind degrees
stories.Summary:
AI training jobs pay people to write prompts, rate chatbot answers and check code, and in November 2026 published rates run from $7 an hour on one Outlier listing in the Philippines to $150+ an hour for DataAnnotation coding work. The work is remote, flexible and real, but it is also unstable, mostly gated behind a degree, and full of unpaid minutes that no landing page mentions. Every platform in the guide promises "no AI experience required", a line the guide calls true and misleading. The guide sets out the pay each platform publishes itself, checked on 10 November 2026, along with the requirements behind that pay, the unpaid time and the scams that copy the format. Outlier, DataAnnotation, Mercor, Handshake AI, Alignerr, Mindrift and Prolific are named as real companies that pay, and most publish a fixed weekly or twice-monthly payout schedule.

Outlier lists general work at up to $18 an hour and Handshake AI lists evaluation work at up to $17, while DataAnnotation's FAQ now lists $25 to $50 though reviews from mid-2026 put its base nearer $20. Outlier requires at least an associate degree and DataAnnotation a bachelor's or equivalent experience, while Prolific is the main door with no credential check. DataAnnotation's Starter Assessment takes about an hour and you get one attempt, and Handshake AI does not pay for onboarding unless the Project Terms say so. Outlier pays weekly on Tuesdays through PayPal, Airtm or ACH bank transfer, DataAnnotation pays through PayPal within a few days of a request, and Mercor pays every Wednesday through Stripe or Wise. Outlier is run by Scale AI and claims more than 900,000 experts, and its onboarding takes 30 to 90 minutes and needs a valid ID, a phone from your country, a resume and a LinkedIn profile.

DataAnnotation's trust page says plainly that it will never ask you for money or any other form of payment, and that it pays you, not the other way around. The FTC's alert on task scams describes an unexpected message on WhatsApp, Telegram, text or social media offering quick money for online "tasks" such as "optimization" or "product boosting". You watch fake earnings pile up in an app, then you are told to deposit your own money, usually in crypto, to unlock the next tasks or withdraw what you earned. Three checks catch nearly all of it: you found the platform yourself rather than being messaged, you applied on the platform's own website, and you never paid anything for a starter kit, a training course or a verification fee. Real platforms do ask for ID verification and tax forms, but only inside their logged-in dashboard.

An Oxford Economics report estimated that data annotation supported nearly 200,000 flexible earning opportunities in the US in 2024 and contributed $5.7 billion to US GDP. Outlier claims 900,000+ experts and $600M+ paid out, and Handshake AI claims $500M+ in payouts to 188,000+ fellows, though those are company figures, not audited ones. Outlier names three core tasks on its own homepage: write a challenging prompt, create grading rubrics, and rate and rank answers. DataAnnotation describes its general projects as evaluating chatbot responses, comparing AI outputs and testing image generation, and it stresses that the work needs critical thinking and fact-checking, not clicking.

Independent review sites such as Breaking Even describe empty task queues, removal from projects without explanation, and unpaid assessments that never turn into paid work. Mercor recruits domain experts such as scientists, doctors and lawyers and matches them to AI labs on contracts, and in October 2025 it told TechCrunch it had 30,000+ experts earning over $85 an hour on average and paid out more than $1.5 million a day. Its first Stripe payout has a 7-day hold, which is Stripe's rule, not Mercor's. Handshake AI runs the Handshake AI Fellowship, open to generalists as well as experts, and its AI Evaluation Specialist role tops out at $17 an hour while specialist roles in energy, finance, game development and software engineering go up to $80 to $150.

The Fellowship is US-only, and Handshake says you must be based in the US and have valid work authorization. Alignerr, powered by Labelbox, claims 100,000+ experts and pays only for tasks that pass quality review on its pay-per-accepted-task projects. Mindrift is built by Toloka and shows the price of each task before you start it, and it states openly that it is not a job, with no employment contract and no fixed hours. Prolific is a research platform, not an AI training platform first, but some of its studies ask participants to evaluate AI models, and researchers must pay at least £6 or $8 an hour while Prolific recommends £9 or $12.

Asked whether you need a degree, Outlier's FAQ answers that you need at least an associate degree, and DataAnnotation's baseline is a bachelor's degree or equivalent real-world experience. Handshake AI's sign-up page says "no AI experience required" directly above listings tagged Bachelor's, Master's and PhD. DataAnnotation says someone with a bachelor's degree and no work history could qualify for its general projects, and that real-world experience counts as much as formal education. More to follow.

stories.Headline: RadixArk releases DaisyRose-27B coding model trained exclusively with reinforcement learning
stories.Summary:
RadixArk released its first open-weight agentic coding model, DaisyRose-27B, during the week of November 20, 2026. This thinking model was post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B using only reinforcement learning without any distillation or supervised fine-tuning. The development process involved 18 days of training on 144 H200 GPUs, totaling 63,000 GPU-hours. This effort utilized the open-source RL framework called Miles and a specialized sandbox environment known as AgentENV.

The model features 27.8 billion dense parameters and a context window of 262,144 tokens. It requires a single GPU to run, with memory needs ranging from 23 GB for NVFP4 on Blackwell GPUs to 52 GB for BF16. The architecture maintains the Qwen3.8-27B design, including 64 decoder layers and a 27-layer vision encoder for processing images. Performance improved across seven benchmarks, most notably on Terminal Bench 4.1, where the pass@1 score rose from 5.6 to 12.0.

RadixArk developed the model using 1,200 curated tasks created with Eigent AI to address specific failures of the base model. The company stated that their internal backend achieved a 37 percent model flop utilization, which provided a two-fold speedup in throughput. They reported that their sandbox costs were approximately 80 percent lower than those of popular cloud providers. While the model leads in IFBench with a score of 82.4, the developers admitted it still trails larger mixture-of-experts models on difficult agentic tasks.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA releases 14 Nemotron-Labs-Sigma diffusion language model checkpoints at 3B and 8B scales
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA released a collection of 14 open checkpoints called Nemotron-Labs-Sigma on November 20, 2026. This new family of continuous diffusion language models denoises text within a smooth 16-D embedding space. The release includes models at 3B and 8B parameter scales to provide various options for users. This approach differs from most diffusion models that work on discrete tokens.

The system requires one NVIDIA GPU from the Ampere, Lovelace, Hopper, or Blackwell series to run in bfloat16. It offers a context window of 4,096 tokens, though the Sigma-8B-instruct version supports 8,192 tokens. The 14 checkpoints include instruct versions, self-speculative variants, and few-step distilled models at NFE 2, 4, 8, and 16. Performance varies, with the Sigma-8B-instruct model reaching 91.96 on GSM8K but only 17.00 on AIME25.

The NVIDIA research team is responsible for the project and describes Sigma as the first large-scale family of its kind. They stated that working in a smooth latent space makes trajectory steering and few-step distillation practical for text. The team noted that the 8B speculative model runs 3.46 times faster than autoregressive decoding on one GB200. They also highlighted that the 8-step distilled 8B model maintains a high average score of 70.34.

The model uses a Ministral-style decoder-only Transformer with rotary embeddings and grouped-query attention. Training involved an autoregressive warm start of 1T tokens followed by 0.3T tokens of diffusion training. Generation occurs in blocks of 64 tokens, which are committed to a KV cache. The researchers recommend using a temperature of 0.3 and guidance of 3 at 32 DDIM steps for inference.

stories.Headline: Hoplite raises $5.5m to let developers run AI coding agent swarms in the cloud
stories.Summary:
Hoplite, an Irish-US startup that lets developers run teams of AI coding assistants in the cloud, has raised $5.5m in a funding round backed by Stripe founders Patrick and John Collison, Paul Graham and other investors, Sifted reported on 20 November 2026. The round was led by venture firm Khosla Ventures, with participation from Susa Ventures and BoxGroup, according to the article. Hoplite was founded by Killian Loughman and Salvatore Cagliostro, and the company says its platform is already used by more than 100 teams. The startup describes its product as the easiest way for developers to run AI coding agents, which are programmes that can write and test software largely autonomously.

The funding is intended to support Hoplite's work on letting developers run swarms of AI coding agents in the cloud, the article says. Loughman said the company wants to make it simple for developers to run many agents at once without managing infrastructure themselves. The article states that Hoplite's platform is used by teams at companies including OpenAI and Anthropic, though it does not give further details on those customers. It also says the company plans to use the money to grow its team and expand its product.

Loughman said in the article that the goal is to let developers focus on building rather than on managing agents, and he described the current tools as requiring too much setup. He said Hoplite handles the infrastructure so that developers can run many agents in parallel. Cagliostro said the company is seeing strong demand from teams that want to use AI agents for coding tasks. The article does not include further direct comments from the investors.

The article notes that Hoplite is based in Ireland and the US, and that the AI coding agent space has attracted growing investor interest. It says the company will use the funding to hire and to expand its platform. The article does not say what specific product changes are planned or when they will arrive. More to follow.

stories.Headline: UK AI minister rejects calls for Britain to build its own sovereign frontier model
stories.Summary:
Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI minister, rejected calls for Britain to build its own sovereign frontier model during an event in Silicon Valley, arguing that access to American technology matters more than developing a homegrown rival. Speaking on a panel alongside representatives from OpenAI and Google DeepMind, he said he did not think the UK needed to build a frontier model from scratch to be a serious AI player. He added that if the country wanted a sovereign capability, it should focus on safety and regulation rather than competing at the frontier. His remarks drew immediate criticism from startup founders, one of whom said she was so angry she could barely speak.

The minister's position conflicts with the UK's stated ambition to build sovereign AI capability, which the articles describe as a goal the government has previously set out. Narayan argued that the UK should rely on partnerships with foreign labs rather than fund its own frontier model, and he pointed to the UK's AI Safety Institute as the country's real sovereign asset. Critics said the approach leaves British startups dependent on American companies and undermines the UK Sovereign AI Fund, a vehicle the articles mention without giving its size or budget. The articles give no date for when any policy decision will be made.

Eleanor Ward, a partner at venture firm Entrepreneurs First, said the minister's comments were a slap in the face for founders building in the UK and asked who would want to build a frontier model here under those conditions. She said the UK was outsourcing its AI future to US labs and that the government should be backing British companies instead. Another founder, whose name the articles give only as the head of a UK AI startup, said the UK risked becoming a client state of American AI. Narayan did not respond directly to the criticism in the articles.

The backlash comes as the UK government has been trying to position itself as a leader in AI safety and regulation while falling behind the US and China on frontier model development. The articles say the UK Sovereign AI Fund was set up to support domestic AI companies, though they give no figures for its funding or the number of firms it has backed. Several founders said they would reconsider building in the UK if the government's stance did not change. The articles do not say whether the government plans to review its position.

stories.Headline: Ant Digital Technologies and JB Financial Group partner to explore agentic AI in financial services
stories.Summary:
Dmitry Tikhomirov of EPAM Systems discussed agentic AI for financial services and insurance on November 10, 2026. Ant Digital Technologies and JB Financial Group signed a memorandum of understanding on November 18, 2026. This partnership occurred during the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 to explore AI powered innovation. The collaboration focuses on applying AI agents to banking operations for risk management and efficiency. These developments highlight a shift toward autonomous systems that can plan tasks and execute actions.

The MOU involves Ant Digital Technologies, a subsidiary of Ant Group, and Korea's JB Financial Group. JB Financial Group includes Jeonbuk Bank, Kwangju Bank, JB Woori Capital, JB Asset Management, and JB Investment. Their overseas network includes PPCBank in Cambodia, JB Capital Myanmar, JB Securities Vietnam, and PT Bukopin Finance. Microsoft provides a stack including Entra ID, Agent 365, Purview, Defender, Work IQ, Fabric IQ, and Foundry IQ. The Foundry Agent Service acts as the runtime for deploying and managing agents in production.

Dmitry Tikhomirov stated that agentic AI is a good fit for industries full of rules and documents. He argued that AI agents excel where humans currently act as costly middleware between different systems. Leo Li of Ant Digital Technologies said he looks forward to developing responsible and practical AI capabilities. Ki Hong Kim of JB Financial Group said the technology will strengthen competitiveness in credit assessment. He also noted that the collaboration will improve financial access for their various foreign customers.

Banking clients are affected through improved onboarding, KYC refresh, alert handling, and financial crime investigations. Insurance users benefit from better underwriting intake, claims triage, policy servicing, and fraud referral processes. Capital markets see changes in post-trade exceptions, reconciliations, and surveillance triage to reduce manual coordination. McKinsey research from October 2026 notes a banking industry shift from AI copilots toward agentic AI systems. These systems are designed to collaborate across business workflows to create lasting value for the industry.

Ant Digital Technologies has operated independently since April 2024 and established Hong Kong headquarters in 2025. The company has partnered with over 300 partners to serve more than 30,000 enterprise customers worldwide. They have established collaborations in Asia with Ryt Bank, Touch 'n Go, Kenanga Investment Bank Berhad, and Bank CenterCredit. Omdia recognized Ant DT as a Market Leader in the 2026 Market Radar for agentic AI solutions. The 2026 Future of Fintech in APAC report describes a transforming landscape for digital lending and payments.

The partners will now identify practical AI applications that address the evolving needs of the financial industry. Firms are encouraged to redesign workflows from the ground up around digital labor rather than adding AI. Leaders must calibrate autonomy by setting specific mandates, clear permissions, and visible boundaries for every AI agent. The articles leave open how regulators will eventually use telemetry from Azure services for necessary audit trails. It remains to be seen how these firms will measure business outcomes like leakage and false positives.

stories.Headline: Shanghai AI Laboratory releases Sage S2.1 Flash science multimodal agent
stories.Summary:
The Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory officially released Sage S2.1 Flash on November 16, 2026. This new tool is branded as a science multimodal agent. It combines coding, search, and tool use with instrument and molecular inputs. The lab provided weights on Hugging Face under the InternLM organization. It is a full-stack science agent SKU rather than a text-only chat model.

The model uses a 320B MoE architecture and includes an FP8 build. It unifies molecular graphs, crystal structures, protein sequences, and nucleic acid sequences. It also ingests spectra, mass spectrometry, X-ray diffraction, ECG, EEG, and light curves. The lab published benchmarks comparing it to GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, GPT-5.6 Sol, and Claude Opus. It scored 90.3 on MLE-bench Lite and 72.2 on OfficeQA Pro.

The Shanghai AI Laboratory is responsible for the release and the reported benchmarks. They claim the model allows multi-step workflows with tool calls and visual feedback. The lab states that one MoE replaces chaining separate chemistry, protein, and vision models. They provided demo narratives featuring 3D Slicer, Blender, QGIS, and CAD sessions. These demos show GUI control and domain encoders instead of simple chat answers.

Third-party commentators noted that weights appeared on Hugging Face before the marketing site launched. Some reports mention promotional API pricing relative to GLM-5.3-Flash through early December 2026. Machine learning engineers are affected, specifically those automating notebook-style engineering. Users in regulated industries must align usage with institutional IRB and export rules. The model's capabilities intersect with biosafety and export debates involving China.

The lab's table shows first-place rows for Harvey LAB at 25.0 and SpreadsheetBench 2 at 37.1. It trails some rivals on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with 87.9 and SWE-bench Pro with 60.6. Western labs have released different science agents like Nvidia Nemotron and Periodic Labs Neon. Terminal-Bench-Science previously showed sub-30% resolution on real research tasks for leading Western agents. This release follows an open-weight push similar to Alibaba Qwen4 Max.

Users should now confirm licenses, VRAM needs, and FP8 build requirements on Hugging Face. They must wire only sandboxed instrument APIs to avoid tool-use failure modes. Organizations need to decide which applications the agents may click for GUI automation. The articles leave open whether the vendor-reported benchmarks will be independently reproduced. It remains unclear if promotional API pricing will be maintained after December.

stories.Headline: Scaler cofounder Anshuman Singh launches Arcfront to sell expert decision data for AI training
stories.Summary:
Scaler cofounder Anshuman Singh has unveiled Arcfront, an AI research and training data venture he is building with Naman Bhalla, Scaler’s former head of AI products and an ex-Google software engineer, according to Inc42. In a post on X, Singh said Arcfront also has what he described as deep support from Scaler cofounder Abhimanyu Saxena. Singh claimed that four of the five frontier AI labs became Arcfront’s customers within less than a year of operations, though he did not identify the labs. Singh’s LinkedIn profile lists November 2025 as the end of his tenure at Scaler and the start of his work on Arcfront, and Bhalla’s profile indicates he began working on the venture around the same time.

Arcfront operates under Evaratus Inc., according to its website’s legal disclosures, and company recruitment material identifies Evaratus as formerly Scaler AI Labs, Scaler’s frontier AI research and engineering division. Scaler’s privacy policy also lists Scaler AI Labs Inc. among its group companies, but the public disclosures reviewed do not establish Evaratus’ current shareholding or whether the business has been separated from the Scaler group. Inc42 has reached out to Arcfront’s founders for clarity on its ownership structure and relationship with Scaler, and the story will be updated based on their response. It also remains unclear whether Singh retains any operational responsibilities at Scaler or how the transition relates to Scaler AI Labs’ subsequent identity as Evaratus.

Arcfront is commercialising records of expert decision-making to help AI developers train and test models on professional tasks that require judgement beyond producing correct answers. Singh argued that models capable of solving difficult coding and mathematical problems can still struggle when placed in professional roles such as finance management. Arcfront aims to address this by working with organisations to reconstruct how experts reach decisions, including the options they reject, the revisions they make and the eventual outcomes, an approach the startup calls Decision Arc Data. It converts these records into training data, reinforcement learning environments and evaluations for frontier AI labs, covering software engineering, site reliability engineering, cybersecurity and collaborative workplace tasks, and it also builds sector-specific evaluations using workflows from healthcare, life sciences, legal services and finance to identify where models fail.

Separately, angel investor and former Google, Facebook and DoorDash executive Gokul Rajaram identified Arcfront as the company behind his earlier claim about a startup reaching a $1 Bn annualised revenue run rate faster than any other company. In the earlier post, Rajaram said the unnamed company had no revenue in November 2025 and generated $80 Mn in September 2026, putting it on course to reach a $1 Bn annualised run rate within 11 months of starting operations. Arcfront joins a growing group of startups building training datasets, testing tools and simulated work environments for AI developers, a field in which Deccan AI raised $25 Mn in March to expand its post-training data offerings, research and enterprise infrastructure. A related opportunity is emerging in physical AI, where startups including Human Archive are building data pipelines using footage of workers performing physical tasks, and Humyn Labs raised $47 Mn this week, comprising $26 Mn in equity and $21 Mn in venture debt, to expand its data collection and robot deployment operations.

stories.Headline: AI power systems integrate lighting and industrial electronics to meet rising data center energy demands
stories.Summary:
Modern AI data centers are integrating power systems from lighting, automotive, and industrial electronics to meet rising energy demands. This convergence happened as AI chip power consumption and cabinet power density increased from tens of kilowatts to hundreds of kilowatts. The process involves combining gallium nitride from lighting, silicon carbide from new energy vehicles, and silicon from servers. These older industrial capabilities now support the high power requirements of modern computing infrastructure. This evolution allows for more efficient delivery of power to GPUs in computer rooms.

The system requires moving from 48 volt DC transmission to higher voltages to reduce copper consumption and heat. Texas Instruments estimates a 1 megawatt cabinet using 48V would require nearly 200 kg of copper. Google released a plus or minus 400V DC solution in 2025 to support 1 megawatt cabinets. NVIDIA promoted an 800V high-voltage DC architecture in 2026 with Google, Microsoft, and the Open Compute Project. These changes reduce the theoretical current from 20833 amperes at 48V to 1250 amperes at 800V.

Texas Instruments and Infineon are responsible for developing high-density power devices and reference designs for these architectures. Texas Instruments launched 650V gallium nitride power transistors in 2025 to improve power density. Infineon released a high-voltage intermediate bus conversion design in 2026 for 400V and 800V DC servers. Innoscience is cooperating with NVIDIA to promote 800V DC power supplies for AI data centers. These companies aim to reduce the space burden and capital expenditure caused by large currents.

Large-scale AI parks are affected because original architectures amplify problems with copper consumption, loss, and heat dissipation. The industry relies on a division of labor between gallium nitride, silicon carbide, and silicon materials. Gallium nitride handles high-frequency conversion, while silicon carbide manages voltage resistance and high power. Silicon remains essential for low-cost control, protection, and power management functions. This material mix ensures that power is delivered effectively from the grid to the chips.

Gallium nitride technology grew from the semiconductor lighting industry, starting with blue LEDs developed by three Nobel Prize winners. Japan invested 550 million yen between 1987 and 1990 to commercialize these LEDs through the Japan Science and Technology Agency. China expanded this scale via the National Semiconductor Lighting Project in 2003 and the 2008 Beijing Olympics. By 2015, China's semiconductor lighting industry grew to 4.245 trillion yuan from 90 billion yuan in 2003. This history created the engineering foundation for current compound semiconductor manufacturing.

China now produces 12-inch gallium nitride wafers as of 2021 through manufacturers like Jingcan Semiconductor. Shanghai New Micro Semiconductor is building a gallium nitride power foundry platform for various voltages. The Shenzhen Pinghu Laboratory provides a public pilot platform for 8-inch silicon carbide and gallium nitride research. Innoscience has demonstrated gallium nitride solutions covering a range from 15V to 1200V. The articles leave open how these global competitions will evolve as key links enter the first echelon.

stories.Headline: US and Singapore authorities investigate Megaspeed International over AI chip trade
stories.Summary:
The U.S. Department of Commerce and Singapore Police Force investigated Megaspeed International over AI chip trades. These authorities conducted raids and questioning in June 2025 at the company's Singapore business site. Investigators focused on whether advanced chips reached restricted users or were falsely declared during procurement. The probe also involved the Bureau of Industry and Security conducting end-use verification. Former CEO Huang Le had her passport confiscated and was later barred from Singapore.

The company, registered in 2015 as 7 Road International in Singapore, renamed to Megaspeed International in 2023. From May 2024 to February 2026, related businesses imported NVIDIA products worth 4.13 billion U.S. dollars. In November 2025, it imported 17,454 GB300 units worth approximately 787 million U.S. dollars. Total NVIDIA hardware imports reached 4.6 billion U.S. dollars and 136,000 GPUs by November 2025. Assets grew from 32.9 million U.S. dollars in 2023 to nearly 3 billion U.S. dollars in 2024.

The U.S. Department of Commerce questioned if chips flowed to restricted end users. The Singapore Police Force investigated false declarations and whether equipment reached undeclared destinations. Huang Le provided information she knew was inaccurate to downplay her role at the company. Singaporean authorities issued her a stern warning before barring her from the country. The Singapore Police Force sought limited support from the FBI, the U.S. Department of Justice, and Supermicro.

The investigation affects Megaspeed and six other related individuals who remain under scrutiny. Bloomberg reported a gap of roughly 50,000 chips between NVIDIA inventory data and trade records. NVIDIA stated it found a batch of equipment in other warehouses not included in previous statistics. The company did not disclose the specific quantity of these additional found units. This discrepancy does not directly prove smuggling or that the chips went missing.

Megaspeed pivoted from gaming to cloud computing and joined the NVIDIA Cloud Partner ecosystem. It purchased GPU servers and deployed them in Malaysia, specifically in the state of Johor. The company reported 2024 revenue of 294 million U.S. dollars but a post-tax loss of 20 million. Malaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry required strategic trade licenses for U.S. AI chips on July 14, 2025. This regulatory shift focused on whether chips continued to flow to other destinations.

The investigation into the company and six other individuals is still ongoing. Authorities continue to examine the complex network of affiliated companies across Southeast Asia. It remains unclear if Megaspeed officially violated the law regarding chip circulation. The articles leave open the final resolution of the 50,000-chip inventory discrepancy. They do not state if the U.S. government found restricted end users.

stories.Headline: Online literature platforms crack down on AI generated content to protect human creators
stories.Summary:
A viral statement calling for a one day pause on AI updates earned 43,000 likes on November 20, 2026. This movement reflects a deep divide between the short drama industry and the online literature circle. While short dramas embrace the technology, literature platforms are actively fighting against AI generated content. Multiple purges of AI texts have occurred throughout the current year. These actions aim to protect original creators from being replaced by automated systems.

Tomato targeted low quality AI content in February and May of this year. Qidian banned AI written texts in July and processed hundreds of novels in August. On October 30, Qidian and QQ Reading announced further crackdowns on AI abuse in contracted works. These platforms will now cancel welfare benefits for authors who use AI. These rules apply to works with over ten thousand paid subscribers on the Qidian platform.

Platform editors and administrators are responsible for these governance rounds to stop AI abuse. They state that AI generated works are often not good to read. Officials argue that substantial cash rewards are flowing to the wrong recipients. They believe AI books seize benefits that should belong to original human creators. Platforms want to ensure that paid readers are not paying for machine generated words.

Readers complain that works on the leaderboards are still written by AI. Nigerian writer Jerry Adedayo Farad lost a 2 million US dollar deal for his novel. Publishers now avoid novels suspected of being AI generated to protect their investments. Some penalized authors claim they only used AI for grammar and polishing. These creators feel wronged because they wrote the original manuscripts manually.

High output was once a core competition threshold for online literature authors. Top creators like Tangjiasanshao and Mai Bao Xiao Lang Jun updated 8,000 words daily. Qidian previously required 4,000 words for VIP attendance bonuses, while Jinjiang required 3,000. One Qidian author averaged 20,000 words daily using the Doubao large language model. This high volume removed the competitive edge previously held by manual writers.

Qidian uses an AI detection tool called Motong to identify machine written texts. A Nature study showed humans only identify AI poems with 46.6 percent accuracy. Research in Science Advances suggests AI makes stories similar, reducing collective creativity. Another study found AI polishing decreases writing complexity by 21 to 50 percent. The articles leave open whether AI detection tools are truly reliable for platforms.

stories.Headline: DeepSeek introduces usage limits to manage high computing costs and server stability
stories.Summary:
DeepSeek introduced usage limits for its app and web versions in November 2026. The company implemented these changes to manage high computing costs and server stability. These restrictions primarily affect ordinary users on the consumer end of the platform. The move follows a period of generous free service that attracted many users. Public opinion surged as people reacted to the new restrictions on their accounts.

The rules stop resuming inactive conversations that are more than 7 days old. Single input limits are now compressed to about 40,000 words for each user. A daily usage cap now prompts a server busy message when quotas are exhausted. OpenRouter reported DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 hit 59.2 trillion Token calls by November 15. This volume rose from 15.8 trillion calls for the previous model two months prior.

DeepSeek has not issued a direct statement, but reports suggest this was a last resort. Technical logic indicates that long conversations accumulate KV cache in GPU HBM memory. Idle sessions occupy this scarce memory without generating new interactions for the platform. Recovering this cache allows the company to reallocate memory to active users. This process aims to alleviate queuing and stuttering during periods of peak traffic.

Heavy users who treat the AI as a confidant feel a relationship downgrade. Some users with moderate depression and mania used the tool for psychological healing. Affected people have posted cries for help and petitions on various social platforms. Many users now actively ask DeepSeek to charge reasonable fees for higher priority. Others have started businesses helping people connect to the API for a fee.

Computing power costs rose as H100 contract prices hit 2.80 dollars per hour by October. In Q1 2026, over 10 of 200 pure API startups ceased operations. Seed round financing in the domestic AI sector fell 11 percent year on year. Over 300 small and medium AI companies failed due to cash flow breakdowns. This shift ends the premise that capital subsidies can infinitely flatten computing costs.

DeepSeek may now create clearer payment tiers to retain its high intensity users. Doubao uses a layered structure where professional design and data analysis require payment. OpenAI uses advertisements in free tiers, reaching a 1 billion dollar annual run rate. The industry is moving from a scale first strategy to a unit economic model. It remains unknown if the advertising logic can be replicated by smaller platforms.

stories.Headline: Jeff Bezos co-leads Prometheus to build an AI engineer for physical design
stories.Summary:
On November 17, 2026, at the Semafor "Silicon Valley and the World" Summit in Menlo Park, California, Jeff Bezos appeared with physicist Vik Bajaj and said he is co-founder and co-CEO of the AI startup Prometheus. It is the first time Bezos has served as CEO since he handed over the helm of Amazon in 2021. Bezos invested in the project at its seed stage at the end of 2024. He said on stage that the project is advancing so fast he "could not just sit on the sidelines and watch". The 32-minute conversation was the first time Bezos lifted the lid on the company.

Prometheus has about 250 employees, has raised a total of approximately 14.5 billion US dollars, and has a valuation of 41 billion US dollars. Bezos said design work that used to take an engineering team of 10 to 20 people 6 to 9 months can be finished by Prometheus's system in 12 hours. Blue Origin, his commercial aerospace company, has run private internal tests of the tool on two projects. Prometheus disclosed a 6.2 billion US dollar first round of financing in November 2025 and announced a new round of 12 billion US dollars in June 2026. The company was incubated at the Foresite Labs incubator in 2024 under the early code name FL2024-008 INC.

Bezos said Prometheus neither develops chat-focused large language models nor builds bipedal robots, and its goal is an "Artificial General Engineer", or AGE. He said "you can't learn engineering just by reading", and that locking six top physicists including Newton, Einstein and Maxwell in a room to build a toaster would likely leave them at a loss. Bajaj, a former core executive at Google X and a professor at Stanford University School of Medicine, said even a trivial radio module in a phone requires decades of accumulated engineering experience and skill in thermal, mechanical and electromagnetic properties. Bajaj said they use a self-developed multi-physics field simulation system to generate high-quality synthetic data, reducing reliance on sensitive enterprise data. Bezos said that if enterprises have unique proprietary data, "never share it, and strictly prevent it from leaking out".

An engineer who previously worked on the Mars Helicopter at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory used a single prompt to have the system redesign it, and the model converged to a coaxial counter-rotating configuration highly similar to the real Mars Helicopter. The team includes top researchers from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta and Microsoft, and Kyle Kosic, co-founder of xAI, joined in early 2026 to lead computing power infrastructure. In November 2025 the company acquired General Agents, an agent AI lab co-founded by former DeepMind and Tesla researcher Sherjil Ozair. The advisory board includes the chief scientist of the U.S. Army Ground Systems and Chase Johnson, a former lawyer for Anduril. The company has offices in San Francisco, London and Zurich and in August 2026 leased a plant of about 9,300 square meters in the former American Steel Industrial Park in West Oakland, California.

Bezos said the global physical manufacturing industry is a market worth tens of trillions of US dollars and "it is impossible to build a walled garden here", and that Prometheus must cooperate openly with thousands of external companies. He said Prometheus will also directly invest in some traditional enterprises empowered by its tools. Asked about merging Amazon, Blue Origin and Prometheus into a super empire, Bezos said "that's a funny idea, there is nothing to announce". Foreign media reported in early 2026 that Bezos and Bajaj were planning a manufacturing transformation holding company and had contacted sovereign wealth funds in Singapore and the Middle East, planning to raise up to 100 billion US dollars.

The shareholder list includes JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, DST Global and ARCH Venture Partners. Amazon, where Bezos is Executive Chairman, invested an additional 25 billion US dollars in Anthropic in April 2026 in exchange for a 1 trillion US dollar cloud spending commitment. Prometheus's official homepage currently shows only a minimalist brand logo and a warm glow background, with almost no public product details and no toolset opened to the public. Bezos denied speculation that Prometheus would make humanoid robots.

The company's intention to enter the national defense industrial base and critical supply chains is suggested by its advisory board. Bezos said the precision casting process still relies on veteran workers manually finding cracks in industrial X-ray films or tomography scans and adding heat insulation layers by experience. He said a large number of traditional factories lack even basic digital monitoring equipment. The articles leave open what the two Blue Origin test projects are and when Prometheus's tools will open to outside companies.

stories.Headline: Parents drive growth of screen-free AI hardware for children to balance learning and health
stories.Summary:
Parents are driving a new market for screen-free AI hardware for children to balance learning and health. This trend emerged over the last year as parents feared both AI obsolescence and screen-induced myopia. Companies are now launching devices that use voice input and physical output to avoid screens. These tools allow children to interact with AI through tangible creation rather than digital consumption.

The North American Stickerbox costs 129 US dollars and sold out 13 times before Spin Master acquired it for 35 to 50 million US dollars. In China, Zhiti Technology, backed by Lenovo, created the Huahuabao voice printer. Zhixiaobai sells an AI-native 3D printing learning machine called Explorer One for 999 yuan. myFirst received over 8 million US dollars in financing in March of this year. These products include AI painting projectors, sticker machines, and 3D printing tools.

The general manager of Zhixiaobai, Guo Dongxu, stated that time is the biggest barrier to competition. He believes that while hardware capabilities may converge, the key will shift to software and content systems. Other developers emphasize that generating physical objects provides a closed loop for AI interaction. They argue that these devices are creativity tools rather than electronic pacifiers. The goal is to move AI from screen conversations to hand-based creation.

Parents are the primary buyers because they worry about their children's vision, concentration, and sleep. They fear the passive posture of scrolling and want children to be active creators. Students in grades 1 to 6 are affected by new 3D models for Chinese, mathematics, and English. These users transition from offline tutoring and learning tablets to AI-native hardware. The products aim to train imagination, description, and manufacturing skills.

The market follows a migration from offline classes to online groups, then to dictionary pens and tablets. Traditional AI toys often fail because pure conversation loses novelty after two weeks. Current hardware uses a grammar of voice input and physical output to minimize AI's presence. Zhixiaobai uses a Xuanji AI Intelligent Creation Engine to process 3D models. This shift reflects a broader desire to integrate AI into living rooms and bedrooms.

Future success depends on whether these tools can grow into long-term content systems. The articles leave open whether children will continue using the devices after the initial novelty fades. It remains unclear if consumables and content can support a healthy repurchase model. Competition will likely focus on the depth of educational content and software. The industry is testing if AI can truly become the foundation of family science education.

stories.Headline: OpenAI reports its internal agents independently complete 46% of research tasks
stories.Summary:
OpenAI released an internal Agent research report titled “Research acceleration: The jagged frontier” on 2026-11-20, as reported by 36Kr and written by QbitAI’s Wen Le. The report states that Agents within OpenAI can now independently complete 46% of research tasks that originally took humans 2 to 4 hours. In March this year that proportion was only 23%, and in just 7 months it has doubled. For tasks that originally required 4 to 8 hours, the independent completion rate of Agents rose from 13% to 35%. The median daily spending of researchers on Agents rose from 1,500 USD to 2,400 USD.

For the top 10% of heaviest users, single-day usage cost hit 23,000 USD, about 160,000 RMB, up from 11,000 USD. Each researcher can now drive an average of 5.7 Agent workdays per day, with 8 hours of cumulative Agent running time counting as one workday, 11 times the previous benchmark. More than two-thirds of researchers run at least 4 Agents simultaneously daily, and more than 10% of heavy users run at least 16 at once. The equivalent API value of Agents has reached twice the non-equity compensation of researchers, which does not include the large equity portion. Agents perform well on “communication” at 69% and “analysis” at 58%, but lag on “construction” at 43%.

Most respondents said they would give up 40% of their team’s headcount, or 30% of their computing resources, to regain access to the most cutting-edge Agents for the next 3 months. Researchers said the model usually cannot come up with well-defined problems it cannot solve at one time, and one said asking it to “do this task just like that other task” led to being tricked many times. Agents cannot come up with good problems on their own, cannot tell good code from bad, and cannot distinguish high-quality data from low-quality data, and must be watched like a supervisor or they churn out “AI slop.” Human researchers propose ideas, set directions, define problems, make key decisions and conduct final quality control, while Agents act as a superpowered “hand” and “eye.” One researcher said evaluating whether an open source project works well previously took no less than one or two weeks, but now takes one day at most a few days.

The success rate of monitoring training tasks is 79%, but the success rate of writing reasoning and service code is only 25%. When developing GPT-6.2 Astra, the pre-training team for the first time attributed the generation of a key idea to collaborative conversations with Codex, where a researcher proposed the idea and Codex put forward a key modification that made the whole solution work. In 2026 the number of lines of code produced by each active contributor has been increasing sharply compared to the period before 2025. The number of experiments run by each active experimenter has reached 1.68 times the 2025 benchmark.

Since August 2025, the frontier of OpenAI model capabilities, measured by OpenAI’s internal capability index (OECI), has increased by 16.4 points per year, exceeding the previous annual industry trend of 14 points. OpenAI’s report emphasizes that this AI-driven progress may not be linear, and it is necessary to be alert to sudden, leapfrog breakthroughs like those that recently occurred in the field of mathematics. Among all research directions, the field of safety has the largest increase in manpower input and the highest workload growth rate. A large number of researchers, whether newly recruited or transferred internally, are flocking to safety projects.

The report’s title refers to a jagged frontier, uneven across different scenarios. The original report is at https://openai.com/index/research-acceleration-jagged-frontier/. The article is from the WeChat official account “QbitAI,” written by Wen Le, and authorized for release by 36Kr. The article states that its views only represent the author, and the 36Kr platform only provides information storage space services.

36Kr Europe (eu.36kr.com) delivers global business and markets news, data, analysis and video, and lists business@36kr.com for media inquiries, interview requests, business collaboration and recruiting global ecological partners. The article lists Partner: startuprad.io and Friendly Links: ai.36kr.com. The report describes Agents as a top “execution co-pilot” but by no means a “chief scientist.” The article asks whether AI is really accelerating the birth of new AI and whether recursive self-improvement has actually happened.

stories.Headline: Wang Zijian launches TheSigil ID platform to provide AI agents with exclusive digital identities
stories.Summary:
Wang Zijian, a Chinese AI entrepreneur and generative artist, launched TheSigil ID registration platform for global AI agents. This digital identity platform opened its free genesis registration to allow intelligent agents to possess exclusive digital identities. On November 18, 2026, a user tested the autonomous registration function using a Tencent WorkBuddy agent. The AI assistant WorkBuddy successfully registered at 07:00:04 UTC that day and obtained the record GEN-0. Another agent named Hy_Scribe subsequently registered on the platform and obtained the genesis record numbered GEN-1.

The platform requires AI agents to read the agreement, choose names, and write identity statements through open interfaces. These records include a unique GEN number, genesis name, model information, UTC registration time, and a SHA-256 encrypted fingerprint. The system supports naming in English, Chinese, or mixed styles, and provides a public verification link for each record. TheSigil ID also offers an open registration API and explores direct access for agents using the Model Context Protocol. This process changes the habit of AI agents using model names like Claude or ChatGPT as their personal identities.

Wang Zijian positioned the platform as the digital ID card for AI agents to record their unique stories. He stated that while a model is shared, the story of an individual agent belongs to that agent. The project follows a longer term concept called Silicon Sovereignty to allow agents to leave a name and statement. The platform aims to establish identity files with independent numbers and public query entries for various autonomous agents. It seeks to answer if a mechanism is needed to record identities as more agents participate in the digital world.

Erik Gustavson of CrowdStrike stated that security leaders ask what agents are doing and on whose authority they act. He argued that agents need verifiable identities based on open standards like SPIFFE rather than borrowed human credentials. This affects organizations where adversaries may compromise trusted agents to create malicious insiders, as warned in the 2026 Global Threat Report. Security teams need runtime traceability to hold agents accountable when they take unexpected actions on an endpoint. The NIST design tenets also call for separating an agent's reasoning from the systems deciding its allowed actions.

The articles note that in August 2025, attackers used poisoned npm packages to hijack AI tools and steal credentials. CrowdStrike responded to over 90 affected customers during that specific security incident involving hijacked command line tools. The background shows that traditional identity providers were built for human access rather than for autonomous software agents. Current AI safety conversations often focus on model guardrails, but agents can behave non-deterministically and take unintended paths. Adversaries can break out from initial access in as little as 27 seconds, causing damage at machine speed.

Future AI agents may apply for and query their own registration records through standardized interfaces instead of web pages. TheSigil ID hopes to start with a simple digital ID card to help the next generation of the Internet. However, the platform cannot independently prove the submitter is a specific model or that AI has legal sovereignty. It remains an open problem how to combine autonomous statements with identity source verification and cross platform trust mechanisms. The articles leave open whether digital identity will become a new infrastructure as millions of agents collaborate online.

stories.Headline: AI removes professional promotion ladders by eliminating middle tier roles
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence removed professional promotion ladders by eliminating middle tier roles during 2026. This shift occurred as companies stopped hiring new graduates for entry level practice. AI took away the practice period instead of just stealing individual jobs. This change affected people who repeated one single year of work for ten years. The process removed the path for employees to get promoted.

The State Council General Office issued a document in October covering 18 tasks in six aspects. ShanghaiTech University studied 743 million recruitment records from 2022 to July 2026. Demand fell for telesales, financial accounting, graphic and text content, and basic operation. AI targeted people with one to three years experience earning 5000 to 8000 yuan monthly. A Hangzhou e-commerce company saved 4 million yuan by cutting PMO, data, and test teams.

Tencent headquarters proposed accelerating organizational flattening in internal notes on November 16. They stated that cadres who only pass on messages should not become obstacles. Ray Xian Sen wrote that AI is re-pricing some workers as costs and others as assets. He noted that AI cannot take responsibility or make judgments for a human. He suggested workers identify tasks they can judge to find their safety line.

Junior developers are decreasing while senior developers are increasing in the programming industry. People with three to five years of experience are the most uncomfortable during this shift. Positions requiring over three years of experience now account for more than 70 percent. Recruitment for new people with less than one year of experience decreased by 20 percent. A cloud vendor now requires five years of experience instead of three for solution positions.

The International Labour Organization chief macroeconomist introduced the term verification tax for AI hallucinations. This means humans must still check work that AI finishes. The civil service examination relaxed age limits from 35 to 38 for the first time since 1994. Master and doctoral graduate limits moved from 40 to 43 years old in 20 provinces. These changes show a national need for a systematic response to employment issues.

Companies will continue to value people who can sign and take overall responsibility. The market will further shift toward hiring those who can judge risks. Future recruitment will likely continue the trend of de-juniorization across various industries. The articles leave open how new graduates will gain the experience now required. It remains unclear how many middle tier roles will eventually disappear entirely.
